first_choose_when: Use Vaultwarden for self-hosted, open-source password management with full data control; choose 1Password or LastPass when you want a proprietary cloud password manager with polished UX and enterprise support.
first_notes: Closed-source, subscription-based, and cloud-dependent; convenience vs. control tradeoff.

first_choose_when: Choose @ngneat/falso when you need a modern tree-shakeable TypeScript fake-data library.
first_notes: Modern tree-shakeable TS fake-data library positioned as a lighter, individually-importable alternative; smaller locale/namespace surface than Faker.

first_choose_when: Choose Cipher when MCP-based memory across IDEs and CLIs matters more than Claude-only hooks.
first_notes: MCP-based memory layer for coding agents (works across IDEs/CLIs via MCP); broader client support than a single-tool plugin.

project_or_alternative: `/guard-secure`, `/guard-threat-model` style security skills in a personal/team skill stack
first_choose_when: Choose harness-native security gates when enforceability and trusted curation matter more than breadth.
first_notes: Hand-curated, harness-native security gates you already trust and can enforce in hooks; far narrower coverage. This pack trades enforceability and curation for 800+ ready-made domain workflows.

first_choose_when: Choose the upstream project when English copy and the original rubric matter.
first_notes: The English original this repo translates. Pick upstream for English copy; pick Humanizer-zh for Chinese-language tells and examples.

first_choose_when: Choose cake or SQM when bufferbloat latency under load is the main problem and the shaper can live on the router.
first_notes: Better for router/OpenWrt setups, not a quick per-host script.

first_choose_when: Choose diffusers when you need a maintained library for modern diffusion generation with pretrained pipelines.
first_notes: Maintained library for **diffusion** models (the modern default for generation) with pretrained pipelines and a real API; solves today's generation problem, but a different model family and not a from-scratch reading aid.

first_choose_when: Choose CLI tools when the job is interactive DNS debugging from a shell, not in-process Python logic.
first_notes: Full-featured for humans, but a subprocess to parse rather than a typed Python API.

first_choose_when: Choose elasticsearch-py when you need the official low-level client and current home of the DSL.
first_notes: The official low-level client — and now the **home of this DSL** (`elasticsearch.dsl`). For new code this *is* the answer; the standalone repo is its archived ancestor.

first_choose_when: Choose getdns bindings when stub-resolver and DNSSEC features from the getdns C library justify a native dependency.
first_notes: Smaller Python ecosystem than dnspython and more native-library coupling.

first_choose_when: Choose Unix CLI primitives when you need scriptable pipelines with no GUI.
first_notes: Scriptable Unix primitives, no GUI; better for pipelines, worse for "I just need to eyeball this once."

first_choose_when: Choose native MEMORY commands when you need per-key or instance introspection on a live server.
first_notes: Native commands for per-key/instance memory introspection on a live server; precise per key but you must already know which keys to ask about.

first_choose_when: Choose OpenSearch clients when you run OpenSearch rather than Elastic's distribution.
first_notes: The OpenSearch fork's clients; use these if you run OpenSearch rather than Elastic's distribution.

first_choose_when: Choose redis-cli bigkeys/memkeys when you need built-in live sampling with no dump file.
first_notes: Built into Redis, runs live and needs no file, but only *samples* and adds load to the server; no per-prefix breakdown or report UI.

first_choose_when: Choose plain `requests` plus stdlib futures when an explicit small thread/process pool is clearer than another dependency.
first_notes: No extra dep and no monkeypatching, with slightly more boilerplate than `grequests.map()`.

first_choose_when: Choose `socket.getaddrinfo` when zero dependencies and OS resolver behavior matter more than DNS protocol control.
first_notes: Uses `/etc/hosts` and system config, but only covers basic forward host-to-address lookups.

first_choose_when: Choose `subprocess` plus `ssh` when zero Python dependencies are worth managing process readiness yourself.
first_notes: Keeps OpenSSH behavior, but you own text parsing, child lifecycle, and failure handling.

first_choose_when: Pick system `ssh` when zero Python dependencies and exact OpenSSH parity matter more than robust Python APIs.
first_notes: Zero Python deps and full OpenSSH parity, but fragile (text parsing, quoting, host-key prompts) and requires the `ssh` binary present.

first_choose_when: Choose `tcconfig` when richer scripted rules such as per-IP, per-port, loss, or delay matter more than one Bash file.
first_notes: More featureful over `tc`, but brings a Python dependency.

first_choose_when: Choose `trickle` when you only need to limit one userspace process and want to avoid root-level `tc`.
first_notes: LD_PRELOAD per-process shaping, not a NIC-wide cap.

first_choose_when: Choose woff2/sfnt2woff CLIs when you only need single-purpose format conversion.
first_notes: Single-purpose format converters; fontTools covers the same conversions plus full table manipulation and subsetting.

first_choose_when: Choose zkCli.sh when you need the always-available scriptable ZooKeeper client.
first_notes: Ships with ZooKeeper, scriptable, always available — but raw CLI, no tree visualization, slower for browsing/onboarding.

first_choose_when: Choose a blocking Lua client only for plain Lua programs outside NGINX workers.
first_notes: It blocks, which is the opposite of the non-blocking cosocket design needed inside NGINX.

first_choose_when: Perl-based search tool optimized for programmers.
first_notes: ack is slower and requires Perl; ripgrep is faster, Rust-native, and has broader platform support.

first_choose_when: Pick acme.sh when you want a pure-shell ACME client with a tiny footprint and many DNS APIs.
first_notes: Pure-shell ACME client, zero language runtime, tiny footprint, huge DNS-API list; less "official," no config-rewriting nginx/apache installer — you wire the cert in yourself.

first_choose_when: Keep ad-hoc checks only for trivial throwaway cases; choose django-rules when the same authorization logic needs names, composition, reuse, and tests.
first_notes: The status quo django-rules replaces — no dependency, but scattered, untested, and easy to get subtly wrong.

first_choose_when: Pick AdalFlow when you want a smaller PyTorch-like LM app library with a similar optimize-don't-hand-prompt philosophy.
first_notes: "PyTorch-like" library for building & auto-optimizing LM apps; closest in philosophy (optimize, don't hand-prompt), smaller ecosystem.

first_choose_when: Choose AI-Scientist when you need a heavier idea-to-experiment-to-paper agent-science pipeline.
first_notes: A heavier end-to-end "agent does science" pipeline (idea→experiment→paper write-up); broader scope and far more moving parts than this single-file training loop.

first_choose_when: Choose aider when you need a mature, model-agnostic terminal pair-programmer for git-aware edits.
first_notes: Mature, model-agnostic terminal pair-programmer focused on git-aware edits across many providers; lighter and longer-lived, but not a Codex-derived sandboxed harness-switching runtime.

first_choose_when: AI pair programming assistant with diff-based edits.
first_notes: Aider manages file edits and diffs; RTK focuses on compressing shell command output, not code edits.

first_choose_when: Choose Aider, OpenHands, or SWE-agent when you need general autonomous coding agents with their own loops.
first_notes: General autonomous coding agents with their own models/loops; not Claude-Code-CLI wrappers and not built around the dual-condition `EXIT_SIGNAL` gate.

first_choose_when: Choose aio-pika when you need an async-native AMQP client for `asyncio`.
first_notes: Better async ergonomics, RabbitMQ-only, and smaller in scope than Kombu's multi-transport model.

first_choose_when: Choose aiodns or pycares when async lookup speed is enough and you do not need dnspython's full record/message model.
first_notes: Thin C-Ares lookup layer, not a zone/DNSSEC/custom-message toolkit.

first_choose_when: Choose aiohttp when the app is already asyncio-native or also needs an async HTTP server stack.
first_notes: Mature async ecosystem, but a different programming model than drop-in `requests`.

first_choose_when: Choose aiokafka for async-first Python services that need a native `asyncio` API; choose kafka-python for synchronous consumers, producers, and admin scripts.
first_notes: Native `asyncio` Kafka client (built on kafka-python's lineage); the right pick for async-first apps, narrower surface than the sync client.

first_choose_when: Choose airtest or Poco when image-recognition UI automation with an IDE is the target.
first_notes: Image-recognition-based game/app UI automation with an IDE; a maintained Chinese-ecosystem alternative for coordinate/image-driven device automation.

first_choose_when: Choose AKHQ when you want a direct Apache-2.0 OSS Kafka web UI substitute with active enough maintenance and a different stack/UX; avoid stalled kafka-ui upstream for fresh installs unless compatibility is proven.
first_notes: Open-source (Apache-2.0) Kafka web UI with similar scope (topics, consumers, Connect, schema registry, ACLs); a direct OSS substitute, different stack/UX.

first_choose_when: Pick AKShare for the same Chinese finance/economics data job when maintenance and catalog breadth matter most.
first_notes: The dominant, actively maintained Chinese open financial/economic data library; far broader catalog and a much larger community — generally the better-maintained choice for the same job.

first_choose_when: Choose alass when you need a Rust subtitle aligner that explicitly handles split synchronization.
first_notes: Rust subtitle aligner that explicitly handles *split* synchronization (variable offsets across the file) — stronger for ad-break/scene desync, ffsubsync's known weak spot.

first_choose_when: Choose Alfred when you need a mature commercial macOS launcher with a huge workflow ecosystem.
first_notes: Mature commercial macOS launcher with a huge workflow ecosystem; actively maintained, no SIP-disable/injection, but its own app (not the native Spotlight bar) and paid Powerpack for advanced features.

first_choose_when: Choose alive-progress when you need animated, visually richer single-bar UX with live spinners.
first_notes: Animated, visually richer single-bar UX with live spinners; smaller ecosystem and integration set than tqdm (no pandas/notebook/pipe story of the same breadth).

first_choose_when: Choose Altcha when you want the closest open-source PoW widget and can assemble the server/dashboard layer yourself.
first_notes: Altcha OSS is PoW-only; ML detection is a paid Sentinel product. Cap bundles instrumentation plus a Standalone server with dashboard.

first_choose_when: Choose Angular CDK stepper when you need Angular-native step-by-step UI flows within the Angular ecosystem.
first_notes: Angular-native stepper component; not a general-purpose tour/overlay library and Angular-only.

first_choose_when: Choose Ansible, Salt, or Puppet when you need declarative fleet configuration with version control and idempotency.
first_notes: Declarative, agentless (Ansible) or agent-based config management for fleets with version control and idempotency; the right tool at scale, but no live interactive UI for ad-hoc one-host triage.

first_choose_when: Choose Anthropic's guide when you want a vendor essay on simple, composable agent patterns rather than a repo.
first_notes: A vendor essay arguing for simple, composable patterns over frameworks; similar spirit, different (and shorter) taxonomy. Hosted article, not a repo.

first_choose_when: Pick built-in agent skills when you prefer the host harness's native skill ecosystem.
first_notes: Native skill ecosystem of the host harness; Taste-Skill is a third-party bundle layered on top and can duplicate or conflict with native design skills.

project_or_alternative: Anthropic / built-in agent skills and slash commands
first_choose_when: Pick built-in skills when you need the platform's native skill ecosystem.
first_notes: The platform's native skill ecosystem; this is a third-party bundle layered on top, so it can duplicate or conflict with native design helpers.

project_or_alternative: Anthropic's built-in skills / native slash commands
first_choose_when: Choose built-in skills or native slash commands when you want the platform's own skill surface.
first_notes: The platform's own skill surface; PUA is a third-party persona bundle layered on top and can duplicate or conflict with native behavior.

first_choose_when: Pick native skills when you prefer the platform's own command ecosystem over third-party bundles.
first_notes: The platform's native skill ecosystem; Waza is a third-party bundle layered on top and can duplicate or conflict with native commands.

project_or_alternative: Anthropic's built-in subagent docs / hand-rolled agents
first_choose_when: Choose built-in docs or hand-rolled agents when you need the native way to author subagents yourself.
first_notes: The native way to author subagents yourself. This repo is a third-party starter set layered on that same mechanism, so it can duplicate or collide with agents you've already written.

first_choose_when: Choose built-in agent examples when platform-native personas should avoid third-party overlap.
first_notes: The platform's own subagent examples; Agency-Agents is a third-party bulk catalog layered on top, so names and roles can overlap or duplicate native ones.

first_choose_when: Choose first-party Agent Skills when platform-native behavior matters more than a personal bundle.
first_notes: The platform's first-party skill ecosystem; Khazix's is a third-party personal bundle layered on top and can duplicate or conflict with native skills.

project_or_alternative: Anthropic's official Claude Code skills / built-in commands
first_choose_when: Choose official Claude Code skills when platform-native behavior matters more.
first_notes: The platform's native ecosystem; TÂCHES is a third-party personal bundle layered on top and can duplicate or conflict with native commands.

project_or_alternative: Anthropic's official skills / built-in slash commands
first_choose_when: Choose official skills or built-in slash commands when you want the platform's own ecosystem.
first_notes: The platform's own skill ecosystem; ljg-skills is a third-party curated bundle layered on top, so it can duplicate or conflict with native skills.

project_or_alternative: Anthropic's own context-engineering guidance / built-in skills
first_choose_when: Choose first-party Anthropic guidance when native platform behavior matters more than a third-party corpus.
first_notes: The platform's first-party docs and native skills; this is a third-party corpus layered on top, so it can duplicate or conflict with native guidance and must be reconciled.

first_choose_when: Choose Anubis when you need a reverse-proxy or site-wide PoW gate against scrapers and AI crawlers.
first_notes: Different scope: entry gate vs per-action challenge. The two are complementary, not substitutes.

first_choose_when: Use RustDesk for self-hosted, open-source remote desktop; choose AnyDesk when you want a lightweight, fast proprietary remote desktop with a free tier for personal use.
first_notes: Lightweight proprietary remote desktop with a free personal tier; fast and simple but closed-source and cloud-dependent.

first_choose_when: Choose Airflow, Celery, or cron when you need general-purpose scheduling rather than Scrapy-native deployment.
first_notes: General-purpose schedulers — broader scope, but no Scrapy-native eggify/deploy/version model; you build the spider-running glue yourself.

first_choose_when: Choose APISIX when etcd-backed stateless nodes, fast dynamic reload, and a broader OSS plugin bundle matter more than Kong's commercial ecosystem.
first_notes: Also OpenResty/Lua but configures via etcd (stateless nodes, fast dynamic reload) and bundles more plugins in OSS; smaller commercial/portal ecosystem than Kong.

first_choose_when: Choose Avro when schema-based serialization in data/Hadoop ecosystems is the deciding constraint.
first_notes: JSON-defined schemas and RPC support, but not wire-compatible with Thrift.

first_choose_when: Choose Apache Curator when you need a Java client library for programmatic ZooKeeper access.
first_notes: A Java client *library* for programmatic ZK access (recipes, leader election) — for building, not for ad-hoc GUI inspection.

first_choose_when: Pick Superset when the job is BI/SQL analytics over warehouses and relational databases.
first_notes: BI/SQL-analytics dashboarding over warehouses and SQL databases; stronger for exploratory reporting and charts, weaker for operational time-series, logs, traces, and on-call alerting.

first_choose_when: Choose official Apache Thrift when canonical multi-language stubs and foundation governance matter more than runtime IDL loading.
first_notes: Heavier because of code generation, but broadly supported and the reference implementation.

first_choose_when: Choose Apache Tika when you need a JVM content-detection/extraction framework across many formats.
first_notes: JVM content-detection/extraction framework (many formats, not just HTML article extraction); actively maintained and far broader — heavier, different focus.

first_choose_when: Choose Appcues, Userflow, or Userpilot when you need commercial no-code onboarding **platforms**.
first_notes: Commercial no-code onboarding **platforms** — segmentation, analytics, targeting, checklists, surveys; not open-source repos, recurring SaaS cost, but solve product-led-growth, not just tour rendering.

first_choose_when: Choose Appium when robust mobile UI automation and element selectors matter.
first_notes: A maintained, general mobile-UI automation framework (Android/iOS) with element selectors instead of hardcoded pixels — the right tool if you actually need robust device automation.

first_choose_when: Choose Apple's stack when Apple Neural Engine integration and OS models are the hard requirement.
first_notes: Best Apple Neural Engine integration and OS-level models on newer iPhones, but Apple-locked, conversion can be painful, no path to Android or generic edge hardware.

first_choose_when: Choose framework upload handlers when uploads are small enough that zero extra infrastructure beats edge offload.
first_notes: Django/Rails/Express can handle it, but the app server absorbs the slow-client cost.

first_choose_when: Choose framework upload handling when uploads are small, rare, and ops bandwidth is the binding constraint.
first_notes: Zero infra beyond your app, but slow clients and retries land on the app server.

first_choose_when: Open-source Firebase alternative with broader language support.
first_notes: Appwrite is also open-source and supports more client languages out of the box; Supabase has deeper Postgres integration and a more mature ecosystem.

first_choose_when: Choose Arcade for a cleaner modern Python 2D API with tilemap and physics helpers; choose pygame when you want the lower-level classic API and larger tutorial base.
first_notes: Modern Python 2D game library built on OpenGL with a cleaner OO API and built-in tilemap/physics helpers; younger and smaller ecosystem.

first_choose_when: Choose ArcGIS Pro when proprietary Esri ecosystem support, extensions, or formats are hard requirements; choose QGIS when open-source desktop GIS and lower licensing cost decide.
first_notes: Proprietary commercial desktop GIS; broader vendor support/ecosystem and licensing cost — the main commercial alternative QGIS substitutes for.

first_choose_when: Choose Argo Workflows when the workload is already Kubernetes-native and each step should run as a pod from YAML/CRDs.
first_notes: Kubernetes-native, container-step DAGs defined in YAML/CRDs; great if everything already runs as pods, but no rich Python operator library and a thinner data-engineering UX.

first_choose_when: Choose arq when your app is already asyncio-first and a lightweight Redis queue is enough.
first_notes: Good async ergonomics, but minimal compared with Celery's routing, beat, and canvas.

first_choose_when: Choose ascii-magic when you need a maintained Python image→ASCII library with colour, HTML, and terminal output.
first_notes: Maintained Python library for image→ASCII with colour/HTML/terminal output; properly licensed and far more featureful — the practical replacement.

first_choose_when: Choose ascii-magic / cowsay when you need niche image-art or speech-bubble character generators.
first_notes: Niche art generators (images / speech-bubble characters); narrower and stylistically specific.

first_choose_when: Content-focused static site builder with islands architecture and multi-framework support.
first_notes: Astro is better for static content sites and mixed-framework projects; Next.js is better for dynamic, full-stack React applications with heavy interactivity.

first_choose_when: Pick Async PRAW when the same Reddit API wrapper model must run in asyncio pipelines.
first_notes: The same project's asyncio variant; better for concurrent/streaming workloads, at the cost of async code. Same maintainers.

first_choose_when: Pick AsyncSSH when your codebase is asyncio-native and you want SSH client/server APIs built around `await`.
first_notes: asyncio-native SSHv2 client+server, broad modern algorithm support; better fit for async codebases, but a different (await-based) API and smaller ecosystem of dependents.

first_choose_when: Choose AsyncSSH when the codebase is asyncio-native and SSH forwarding should live inside the event loop.
first_notes: Different API and heavier than a thin Paramiko wrapper, but a better fit for async applications.

first_choose_when: Choose Austin when the job is low-overhead frame-stack profiling rather than live code execution.
first_notes: Observe-only and actively maintained, but a profiling alternative rather than a code injector.

first_choose_when: Choose Authlib when you need a broader and more current OAuth/OIDC/JWT toolkit, especially server-side support; choose Authomatic only when a thin, provider-preset login client is enough.
first_notes: Comprehensive, actively-maintained Python OAuth1/OAuth2/OIDC + JWT library (client *and* server); broader and more current, but a larger API to learn.

first_choose_when: Choose AutoGen when you need a mature conversation-driven multi-agent framework.
first_notes: Mature conversation-driven multi-agent framework; comparable multi-agent scope, different abstractions and a larger community footprint.

first_choose_when: Choose AutoHotkey when you need a Windows-first scripting language purpose-built for hotkeys, macros, and GUI automation.
first_notes: Very mature for Windows automation, but it is its own language and has no native cross-platform/Python story.

first_choose_when: Choose AUTOMATIC1111 when you need the backend SdPaint sits on.
first_notes: The backend SdPaint sits on; can do sketch→image in-browser, but the click-Generate loop is less immediate than live stroke streaming.

first_choose_when: Choose AVQT when you need Apple's proprietary perceptual metric.
first_notes: Apple's proprietary video quality metric; closed implementation, comparable goal but different ecosystem.

first_choose_when: Choose AVQT or proprietary metrics when your workflow requires vendor perceptual metrics.
first_notes: Vendor perceptual metrics (e.g. Apple's AVQT); comparable goal, closed implementations and ecosystems.

first_choose_when: Use cloud transcoders for managed, elastic, pay-per-minute transcoding.
first_notes: SaaS, not a self-hosted framework. Zero ops but vendor lock-in and per-minute cost. Often FFmpeg-derived internally.

first_choose_when: Choose managed cloud transcoders when zero-ops elastic scale matters more than self-hosting.
first_notes: Managed, pay-per-minute transcoding services (often FFmpeg-derived internally); zero ops and elastic scale, but vendor lock-in, per-minute cost, and a SaaS — not a repository you self-host.

first_choose_when: Choose standalone AWS MCP servers when you only need data sources, not packaged skills/playbooks.
first_notes: The underlying AWS MCP servers (docs, pricing, IaC) can be wired up without these plugins; you get the data sources but not the packaged skills, trigger phrases, and guardrails. More assembly, less opinion.

first_choose_when: Choose axolotl for YAML-driven, multi-GPU-first production runs with FSDP/DeepSpeed out of the box.
first_notes: More reproducibility-oriented; LlamaFactory adds web UI and a broader zero-code surface.

first_choose_when: Choose Axolotl when first-class multi-GPU FSDP/DeepSpeed and multimodal support matter after outgrowing one GPU.
first_notes: Stronger for scale-out workflows; Unsloth wins on single-GPU speed and VRAM.

first_choose_when: Use Whisper when you need self-hosted, privacy-preserving, or API-cost-free transcription; choose cloud APIs when you need production SLAs, real-time streaming, and no infrastructure burden.
first_notes: Managed SaaS with real-time streaming, SLAs, and enterprise support. Higher per-minute cost, data leaves your premises, and customization is vendor-gated.

first_choose_when: Pick baostock when you only need free Chinese stock/market history data.
first_notes: Free Chinese stock/market history data; narrower (markets-only) but stable interface.

first_choose_when: Choose bat when you need a `cat` clone with syntax highlighting and paging.
first_notes: A `cat` clone with syntax highlighting and paging; shows Markdown *source* highlighted rather than rendering it, but ubiquitous and fast.

first_choose_when: Choose Bazarr when you need a subtitle management service around Sonarr/Radarr, not just alignment.
first_notes: A subtitle *management* service for Sonarr/Radarr that finds and downloads subs (and can call ffsubsync to sync) — orchestration layer, not the alignment algorithm itself.

first_choose_when: Use Ray Serve when you need Ray-native distributed scaling and deployment graphs; choose BentoML when you want a lighter, container-native model-serving framework.
first_notes: Lighter, container-native model-serving framework; smaller ecosystem than Ray, less proven at very large scale.

project_or_alternative: Bespoke per-library prompting (write your own SKILL.md)
first_choose_when: Pick bespoke prompts when maximum control and zero unused surface justify maintaining every library prompt yourself.
first_notes: Maximum control and zero unused surface, but you rebuild and maintain curated docs for every library yourself instead of installing a vetted bundle.

first_choose_when: Choose bespoke prompts when maximum control and zero unused surface outweigh a large bundle.
first_notes: Maximum control and zero unused surface, but you rebuild and maintain curated, framework-mapped runbooks for every domain yourself instead of installing a vetted bundle.

first_choose_when: Choose BGE/FlagEmbedding when you need the canonical home for newer open embedding checkpoints and rerankers.
first_notes: State-of-the-art open embedding models (incl. strong Chinese); text2vec can load BGE, but FlagEmbedding is the canonical home for the latest checkpoints and rerankers.

first_choose_when: Choose Biome for all-in-one JS/TS formatting and broad linting; choose React Doctor when the deciding need is catching agent-written React anti-patterns.
first_notes: All-in-one Rust formatter+linter; broad JS/TS lint coverage but not focused on catching agent-written React anti-patterns specifically.

first_choose_when: Choose blessed / blessings when you need terminfo-based terminal capability plus cursor and styling control.
first_notes: Terminal capability + cursor/styling library (terminfo-based) — richer terminal control, heavier, less focused on the Windows-ANSI gap.

first_choose_when: Choose blessed or curses when you need lower-level terminal control instead of a widget/animation framework.
first_notes: Lower-level terminal control; `curses` is Unix-only, `blessed` is a friendlier wrapper — neither ships widgets or an animation framework.

first_choose_when: Choose BLIP/BLIP-2 when you need vision-language models that generate text.
first_notes: Vision-language models that *generate* text (captioning, VQA); solve a different problem than CLIP's contrastive embedding/retrieval — not a drop-in substitute.

first_choose_when: Choose BLOSC/blosc2 when you need blocking plus shuffle/bitshuffle meta-compression for numeric arrays.
first_notes: Blocking + shuffle/bitshuffle meta-compressor aimed at numeric arrays; conceptually similar "transform then compress" idea, narrower scope and more mature than OpenZL.

first_choose_when: Choose BMAD-METHOD when you need an agile-agent framework with explicit PM/architect/dev/QA roles.
first_notes: Agile-agent framework with explicit roles (PM/architect/dev/QA); heavier "run a software org" framing GSD deliberately rejects.

first_choose_when: Classic CSS framework with React wrappers.
first_notes: Bootstrap is older and simpler; Ant Design is more modern, component-rich, and better suited for complex data-driven apps.

first_choose_when: Avoid Bootstrap Tour for new work because it is abandoned and unmaintained.
first_notes: Abandoned; was a Bootstrap-dependent tour plugin, no longer viable.

first_choose_when: Choose Braintrust when a commercial experiment platform with hosted scoring, logging, and polished team workflows is worth the managed dependency; choose promptfoo for an open self-run CLI.
first_notes: Commercial eval/experiment platform with hosted scoring and logging; polished team UX. promptfoo trades the managed platform for an open, self-run CLI.

first_choose_when: Choose Brotli when you need strong general-purpose compression for text/web content.
first_notes: Strong general-purpose (esp. text/web) compressor; not format-aware for structured numeric data.

first_choose_when: Pick these only when you must keep an older proxy-based Selenium HAR workflow alive.
first_notes: Older proxy-based HAR capture for Selenium (BrowserMob is Java); similar approach, similarly aging.

first_choose_when: Choose browser-native rich-text compose when you need mail-client built-ins and no extension install.
first_notes: Built into the mail client, nothing to install; but it's WYSIWYG-by-toolbar with no Markdown and weak code-block/table support — exactly the friction Markdown Here removes.

first_choose_when: Choose browser-use when you need a Python browser agent with a batteries-included LLM loop.
first_notes: Python, vision+DOM browser agent with batteries-included LLM loop. Agent Browser is a lower-level Rust CLI primitive (you supply the agent loop), faster to shell out to and MCP-native.

project_or_alternative: Building your own commands from scratch
first_choose_when: Choose custom commands when maximum fit matters more than maintenance burden.
first_notes: Maximum fit, zero lock-in, but you author and maintain every persona and the sequencing yourself.

first_choose_when: Choose built-in compaction when free zero-install summarization is enough.
first_notes: Free and zero-install, but lossy summarization with no structured event ledger, no FTS5 retrieval, and no tool-output sandboxing — exactly the gaps Context Mode targets.

first_choose_when: Choose built-in marketplace skills when native harness equivalents should avoid third-party overlap.
first_notes: The harness's own marketplace skills; Baoyu is a third-party curated bundle layered on top, so it can overlap or conflict with native equivalents.

first_choose_when: Choose the built-in reader mode when zero install and browser-native trust matter more than customization; choose Just Read when per-site selectors, editing, highlighting, or summaries justify an extension.
first_notes: Zero install, baked into the browser; far less customizable, no per-site selectors, no editing/highlighting/summaries.

first_choose_when: Choose built-in retrieval when Claude Code's default file access is sufficient.
first_notes: What Claude Code does by default — high token cost, keyword-shaped retrieval, hallucination on gaps. This skill exists specifically to replace that for doc-heavy tasks.

first_choose_when: Choose Butteraugli when you need Google's perceptual metric from the JPEG XL ecosystem.
first_notes: Google's perceptual metric from the JPEG XL ecosystem; similar lineage but different scoring model and implementation.

first_choose_when: Pick Caddy when adopting a web server that handles ACME automatically is acceptable.
first_notes: A web server that *is* the ACME client — issues/renews transparently with no separate tool; replaces Certbot only if you also adopt Caddy as your server.

first_choose_when: Choose Caddy plugins when automatic TLS and a Go plugin ecosystem matter more than NGINX edge scripting depth.
first_notes: Different language and ecosystem, with less raw ngx_lua-style phase scripting.

first_choose_when: Choose Canal when you need a mature Java MySQL binlog CDC server.
first_notes: Mature MySQL binlog CDC server (Java); more robust and active, but a server to operate rather than a single-binary syncer.

first_choose_when: Choose Canva or 稿定设计 when you need hosted template SaaS rather than a repo.
first_notes: Hosted template SaaS, not a repo — easier for non-agents and richer asset libraries, but closed, no local agent control, no single-file HTML artifact, and far less opinionated visual rigor.

first_choose_when: Choose Casbin when you need a general RBAC/ABAC policy engine and external policy storage; choose django-rules for lightweight in-process Django predicates.
first_notes: Policy-engine with multiple models (RBAC/ABAC) and external policy storage; more general and framework-agnostic, more setup than predicate functions.

first_choose_when: Choose ccusage or token-cost CLIs when you only need focused agent cost reporting.
first_notes: Focused Claude Code/agent token-cost reporters; narrower scope (cost, often one agent) vs. AgentsView's search + analytics + multi-agent.

first_choose_when: Choose the built-in Celery CLI when zero extra process is worth giving up a web UI and REST API.
first_notes: Terminal-only, no at-a-glance fleet view.

first_choose_when: Choose cffi or ctypes for thin C FFI when compiling a custom CPython extension would be unnecessary overhead.
first_notes: Simpler for calling C, but no compiled-speed Python and weaker static typing than Cython.

first_choose_when: Choose chafa when you need a powerful terminal graphics/ASCII/Unicode image renderer.
first_notes: Powerful terminal graphics/ASCII/Unicode image renderer (C); handles colour, animation and many terminals — heavier, far more capable.

first_choose_when: Modular React component library with a focus on developer experience and accessibility.
first_notes: Chakra UI is more "developer-friendly" for custom theming; Ant Design has more enterprise-grade components (especially data tables and forms).

first_choose_when: Choose Chance.js when you need a smaller, older random-generator utility with a narrower catalog.
first_notes: Smaller, older random-generator utility; lighter and dependency-free but a much narrower data catalog and no rich locale system.

first_choose_when: Choose Charles when you need a polished paid native desktop proxy.
first_notes: Paid native desktop proxy; mature, polished GUI for capture/rewrite/throttle, but commercial license and not config-file-driven like whistle's rule syntax.

first_choose_when: Choose Charles or Fiddler when mature desktop GUI debugging is the priority.
first_notes: Mature commercial/freeware GUI debugging proxies; polished UX but closed-source and not scriptable in JS the way AnyProxy's rule files are.

first_choose_when: Choose desktop clients when each person brings their own key and central governance is unnecessary.
first_notes: No central admin, groups, quotas, or shared server.

first_choose_when: Closed-source cloud chat.
first_notes: Proprietary and require cloud; Open WebUI is self-hosted and works offline.

first_choose_when: Choose commercial SaaS when zero-ops vendor management is more important than self-hosting and provider choice.
first_notes: Locked to one model family with the provider holding your data; NextChat trades that convenience for self-hosting, multi-provider choice, and key/data control.

first_choose_when: Choose managed SaaS teams when zero-ops and a single model family are acceptable.
first_notes: HiveChat trades that convenience for self-hosting, multi-provider choice, and key/data control.

first_choose_when: Use RustDesk for self-hosted, open-source remote desktop; choose Chrome Remote Desktop when you want a free, browser-based remote desktop tied to your Google account.
first_notes: Free, browser-based remote desktop tied to Google account; very simple but requires Google ecosystem and offers no self-hosting.

first_choose_when: Choose Chronos when you want the language-model-tokenization approach to time-series forecasting.
first_notes: Tokenizes series into a language-model vocabulary; strong zero-shot forecaster and a direct substitute. TimesFM is decoder-only with native quantile head and (2.5) 16k context.

first_choose_when: The original Windows Clash GUI (archived).
first_notes: The original Clash for Windows project is archived; Clash Verge Rev is the active continuation with a modern Tauri stack.

first_choose_when: macOS-native Clash clients.
first_notes: ClashX is macOS-specific; Clash Verge Rev is cross-platform and actively maintained.

first_choose_when: Closed-source cloud-only assistants.
first_notes: Proprietary and require internet; OpenClaw is self-hosted, MIT-licensed, and channel-agnostic.

first_choose_when: Official Anthropic terminal coding agent.
first_notes: Closed-source, Anthropic-only; Codex is open-source and terminal-native but locked to OpenAI models.

first_choose_when: AI agent with native context management.
first_notes: Claude Code already compresses some output; RTK provides an additional deterministic layer and works across agents.

first_choose_when: Official Anthropic desktop IDE integration.
first_notes: First-party, closed-source; CC Switch adds multi-provider unification but at the cost of a third-party abstraction layer.

first_choose_when: Choose Claude Code or a similar vendor CLI when you need polished terminal coding agents tied to a model family.
first_notes: Polished, vendor-backed terminal coding agents tied to a specific model family; more turnkey but not built around emulating harnesses for arbitrary cheap/open models.

first_choose_when: Choose the general Claude Code Action for broad PR assistance or coding tasks; choose this tool when you specifically need the security-audit prompt and finding filter.
first_notes: Anthropic's general-purpose Claude Action for PRs/coding; not specialized for security audit or finding-filtering.

first_choose_when: Choose Claude Code plugin marketplaces when you need Claude-Code-native plugin distribution.
first_notes: Native Claude Code plugin/marketplace mechanism; richer (commands, hooks, MCP) but Claude-Code-only. Skills targets `SKILL.md` packs across 70+ agents instead.

first_choose_when: Choose built-in Claude Code subagents when native parallel/subagent features are enough and you want no third-party dependency.
first_notes: Anthropic's native subagent/parallel features cover part of OMC's value without a third-party dependency; OMC adds team pipelines, routing, modes, and HUD on top.

project_or_alternative: Claude Code's native skills / built-in slash commands
first_choose_when: Choose native Claude Code skills when you want the platform's own skill ecosystem.
first_notes: The platform's own skill ecosystem; this is a third-party bundle layered on top, so it can duplicate or conflict with native commands.

first_choose_when: Pick the hosted proprietary product when managed cloud polish matters more than local-first/BYOK control.
first_notes: The proprietary hosted product this clones; managed cloud + polish vs Open Design's local-first, BYOK, open-format stance.

first_choose_when: Choose community template collections when you want lighter, à-la-carte Claude Code config snippets.
first_notes: Community config/template collections for Claude Code; lighter, à-la-carte copy-paste vs SuperClaude's installed, coordinated framework.

first_choose_when: Choose claude-flow when you need another Claude-Code multi-agent/swarm orchestration layer.
first_notes: Another popular Claude-Code multi-agent / swarm orchestration layer; overlapping problem space, different abstractions and maturity.

first_choose_when: Choose CLAUDE.md when manual, deterministic project memory is enough.
first_notes: Manual, deterministic, zero-dependency project memory. No background learning or cross-project brain; you curate it by hand. Claude Subconscious explicitly avoids writing here.

first_choose_when: Choose click.style when you need convenient styling inside the Click CLI framework.
first_notes: Convenient styling within the Click CLI framework; Click itself historically depended on colorama for the Windows shim.

first_choose_when: Choose Cline when you want the leaner open-source VS Code coding-agent upstream.
first_notes: Open-source VS Code coding agent; part of Kilo Code's lineage [推断]. Similar in-IDE agent loop; Kilo layers on modes/orchestrator and its own model marketplace. Compare directly if you want the leaner upstream.

first_choose_when: Choose Turnstile when you want managed invisible checks, no client PoW, and Cloudflare network signals.
first_notes: Hosted dependency on Cloudflare; Cap trades that risk-scoring network for self-hosted operation.

first_choose_when: Choose CodeRabbit when you need hosted SaaS that auto-comments on PRs with broad recall.
first_notes: Hosted SaaS that auto-comments on PRs with broad recall; Open Code Review is self-hosted/CLI, precision-biased, and you own the LLM key and posting glue.

first_choose_when: Open-source memory layer for AI agents with graph-based recall.
first_notes: Graph-based memory with a different abstraction; younger and less proven than Mem0.

first_choose_when: Choose collectd when you need an old, lightweight C metrics daemon and accept its aging ecosystem.
first_notes: Old, lightweight C metrics daemon; mature but a smaller, aging plugin ecosystem and weaker modern integrations.

first_choose_when: Choose commercial solving services when a human/hybrid CAPTCHA-solving API is acceptable.
first_notes: Pay-per-solve and no model to host, but ongoing cost, third-party dependency, and the same legal questions.

project_or_alternative: Companion collections (AI product design, UX program mgmt, design leadership, inclusive design)
first_choose_when: Choose the author's companion collections when the task is an adjacent design discipline.
first_notes: Same author's sibling repos in the family; this entry covers only the "design practice" collection. Reach for the others for adjacent disciplines.

project_or_alternative: Computer-use agents (Anthropic computer use / OpenAI Operator)
first_choose_when: Choose computer-use agents when you need vision-based control of a real screen/browser.
first_notes: Vision-based agents that drive a real screen/browser — handle any pixel UI, but slower, costlier, and need a controlled browser/VM, not an in-page snippet.

first_choose_when: Cross-platform package manager for any language, especially scientific Python.
first_notes: Conda handles binary scientific distributions; uv is Python-only and does not replace Conda's binary packaging.

first_choose_when: Choose Conductor, Crystal, or Claude Squad when you need other worktree-parallel Claude Code tools.
first_notes: Other "run parallel Claude Code agents in git worktrees" tools (desktop or TUI). Directly comparable on the core idea; differ in agent breadth (Agent Orchestrator targets 23+ adapters), feedback-loop automation, and maturity — shortlist and compare if you've narrowed to this niche.

first_choose_when: Choose Conduktor when polished UX, enterprise governance, and commercial support outweigh fully open self-hosting; choose kafka-ui only when an OSS browser UI is enough.
first_notes: Polished desktop/web Kafka platform; richer features and enterprise governance, but freemium/commercial — not a fully-open self-hosted OSS UI.

first_choose_when: Choose Confluent Control Center when you are already in Confluent Platform and need deep enterprise monitoring or governance; choose kafka-ui for a lighter standalone dashboard.
first_notes: Deep, enterprise-grade monitoring/governance in the Confluent Platform; commercial and tied to that ecosystem, far heavier than a single-container UI.

first_choose_when: Choose confluent-kafka-python when throughput, latency, Confluent ecosystem integration, or fastest protocol coverage matters most; choose kafka-python when pure-Python portability and trivial installs are the deciding constraints.
first_notes: Official Confluent client wrapping `librdkafka` (C) — highest throughput/latency and quickest protocol coverage, but needs the native lib and is less trivially portable than pure Python.

project_or_alternative: ControlNet scribble in any SD UI
first_choose_when: Choose ControlNet scribble when you need the underlying technique without SdPaint's front-end.
first_notes: The underlying technique SdPaint wraps; available everywhere, but without SdPaint's real-time painting front-end.

first_choose_when: Treat Cozy Drive and Twake Drive as ecosystem choices rather than feature substitutes: use upstream Cozy Drive for Cozy Cloud deployments, and Twake Drive for Linagora/Twake Workplace deployments.
first_notes: This *is* the upstream — Twake Drive is Linagora/Twake Workplace's fork/rebrand of `cozy/cozy-drive`. Same architecture; pick based on which ecosystem (Cozy Cloud vs Twake Workplace) you run.

first_choose_when: Choose cPanel / Plesk when you need commercial web-hosting control panels for vhosts, mail, billing, and reseller accounts.
first_notes: Commercial web-hosting control panels (vhosts, mail, billing, reseller accounts); different problem — managed hosting, not bare OS administration. Proprietary and paid.

first_choose_when: Choose CrewAI when role/crew-based agent orchestration and strong DX matter more than AgentScope's serving stack.
first_notes: Role/crew-based agent orchestration with strong DX; less emphasis on the service/permission/sandbox/observability stack AgentScope ships.

first_choose_when: Choose CrewAI or AutoGen when you need role/conversation-oriented Python frameworks for in-app workflows.
first_notes: Role/conversation-oriented multi-agent Python frameworks for in-app workflows; not single-binary autonomous runtimes.

first_choose_when: Pick specialized frameworks when you want multi-agent teams or RAG-first plumbing without Dify's bundled platform.
first_notes: CrewAI is multi-agent team-oriented; LlamaIndex is RAG-first. Dify bundles both concerns into one platform.

first_choose_when: Choose CRNN + CTC when variable-length text recognition is the real requirement.
first_notes: More capable for variable length, but more to learn and build than this multi-head fixed-length reference.

first_choose_when: Choose crystal or claude-squad when you need multiple parallel Claude Code sessions/worktrees.
first_notes: Run multiple parallel Claude Code *sessions/worktrees*; parallelism is across Claude instances, not across *different vendors' models* reviewing one task.

first_choose_when: Choose CSS transitions/keyframes for simple hover, loading, or one-shot effects; choose Anime.js only when runtime control, sequencing, or dynamic values are needed.
first_notes: Zero JS, GPU-friendly for simple cases; no sequencing, dynamic values, or runtime control. Anime.js is for when you need JS-driven orchestration.

first_choose_when: Choose Cursor when you need a closed-source AI-first *editor* rather than an extension.
first_notes: Closed-source AI-first *editor* (a VS Code fork), not an extension; deeply integrated, paid subscription, no BYOK-at-provider-cost openness. More polished, less open.

first_choose_when: AI-native IDEs with built-in multi-model support.
first_notes: These are full editors with agent features; CC Switch is a meta-manager, not a code editor.

first_choose_when: Choose custom scripts when you need maximum control, scriptability, and no UI.
first_notes: Maximum control, scriptable, no UI; but you rewrite per-task and lose the live visual recipe + Magic detection.

first_choose_when: Hand-rolled `head`, `grep`, `awk` pipelines.
first_notes: Custom wrappers are fragile and per-command; RTK is automatic, supports 100+ commands, and requires no manual piping.

first_choose_when: Choose custom scripts when you only need asset extraction from `.wxapkg`.
first_notes: The `.wxapkg` format is documented enough that ad-hoc scripts exist; viable if you only need asset extraction, not full source restore.

first_choose_when: Choose CyberChef-server when you need the official Node wrapper exposing CyberChef recipes over HTTP.
first_notes: Official Node wrapper exposing CyberChef recipes over HTTP for batch/automation; complements rather than replaces the app.

first_choose_when: Pick Cypress for developer-friendly in-browser E2E on web apps, especially when JS/TS-only is acceptable.
first_notes: Developer-friendly in-browser E2E with time-travel debugging and auto-retry; excellent DX for web apps, but historically Chromium-centric, runs inside the browser's event loop (architectural limits on multi-tab/cross-origin), JS/TS only.

first_choose_when: Pick D2 when its newer language and layout-engine choices matter more than Mermaid's host-platform ubiquity.
first_notes: Newer text-to-diagram language (Go) with multiple layout engines (incl. ELK/dagre) and a focus on cleaner layouts; smaller install base and far less built-in host-platform rendering than Mermaid.

first_choose_when: Choose Dagster when asset lineage, typed orchestration, and local testability are the deciding constraints.
first_notes: Asset-oriented orchestration with typing, data lineage, and strong local testing; more opinionated and newer, with a smaller integration catalog than Airflow's providers.

first_choose_when: Choose Dagster or Prefect for maintained Python-first orchestration instead of adopting an archived Gaia fork.
first_notes: Modern Python-first orchestration with active development and SaaS options; different programming model, maintained — pick over an archived project.

first_choose_when: Choose Darts when you need a modern maintained Python forecasting library with many model families.
first_notes: Modern, maintained Python forecasting library (many models incl. deep learning) with a unified API; production-oriented, far heavier than a teaching script.

first_choose_when: Pick a hosted suite when you want collection, storage, dashboards, and alerting operated for you.
first_notes: Hosted all-in-one (collection + storage + dashboards + alerting); zero infra to run but per-host/per-metric billing and vendor lock-in vs. self-hosted Grafana over your own backends.

first_choose_when: Choose commercial APM when traces, alerting, and fleet-wide observability matter more than a Celery-purpose-built dashboard.
first_notes: Paid and heavier, but broader than Flower.

first_choose_when: Use DaVinci Resolve for professional-grade color, VFX, and editorial — it's a commercial NLE, not an OSS framework.
first_notes: Professional commercial NLE with world-class color grading; free tier exists but not open-source and not embeddable as a library.

first_choose_when: Choose Daytona when you need a dev-environment/sandbox runtime for agents.
first_notes: Dev-environment/sandbox runtime for agents; overlapping use case, different orchestration and feature emphasis.

first_choose_when: Choose dCode or online decoders when browser convenience for one-off transforms outweighs offline privacy.
first_notes: Browser convenience for single transforms; data leaves your machine and no offline/self-host story — the privacy gap CyberChef closes.

first_choose_when: Choose ddddocr when you need a maintained, ready-to-use OCR/CAPTCHA library covering many types.
first_notes: Far more practical today than reviving a 2020 tutorial; use only where you have authorization to solve the CAPTCHA.

first_choose_when: Choose DEAP when you need a flexible low-level evolutionary-computation toolkit.
first_notes: Flexible evolutionary-computation toolkit; very general/low-level, but you assemble more yourself — pymoo gives higher-level, ready multi-objective algorithms and benchmarks.

first_choose_when: Choose Debezium when you need the full Kafka Connect CDC platform.
first_notes: Full CDC platform (Kafka Connect) with connectors, schema history, exactly-once-ish delivery; far heavier — this library is the lightweight, code-it-yourself counterpart.

first_choose_when: Choose Debezium when you need the industrial-strength CDC platform.
first_notes: The industrial-strength CDC standard; durable, multi-source, exactly-once-ish via Kafka — but it's a whole platform to run vs one Go binary.

first_choose_when: Choose DeepEval for Python-native pytest-style evals and deeper RAG metrics; choose promptfoo when language-agnostic YAML suites, model matrices, and integrated red-teaming matter more.
first_notes: Python-native eval framework (pytest-style, metrics like G-Eval/faithfulness); better fit for Python teams and RAG metric depth. promptfoo wins on language-agnostic YAML config, side-by-side model matrix, and integrated red-teaming.

first_choose_when: Choose DeepKE when you need a maintained transformer-based Chinese knowledge-extraction toolkit.
first_notes: Maintained Chinese knowledge-extraction toolkit (NER/RE/attribute), transformer-based; a real library to build on, vs. AgriKG's frozen end-to-end demo.

first_choose_when: Use Whisper; DeepSpeech is effectively abandoned since Mozilla stepped back.
first_notes: Mozilla's older English-centric ASR project. Do not start new projects on it.

first_choose_when: Choose DeepSpeed where the Microsoft ZeRO/offload stack is already the production default.
first_notes: DeepSpeed has the deeper deployment track record; Colossal-AI overlaps on ZeRO/offload but adds its own plugin and Booster surface.

first_choose_when: Pick dehydrated when you want a minimal hook-driven Bash ACME client and accept more DIY wiring.
first_notes: Minimal Bash ACME client (formerly letsencrypt.sh); hook-driven, lightweight, but more DIY and a smaller ecosystem than Certbot.

first_choose_when: Choose Depth Anything V1 only when you have a V1-pinned pipeline.
first_notes: The predecessor; V2 is sharper on fine detail and more robust per the authors — use V2 unless you have a V1-pinned pipeline.

first_choose_when: Choose Devin/Cognition when hosted autonomous-engineer SaaS is acceptable.
first_notes: Hosted "autonomous engineer" SaaS covering a similar manage-the-work pitch; closed, no self-host, no fork. Symphony is OSS and self-hosted but preview-stage.

first_choose_when: Choose DevUtils when you need a polished native macOS-only equivalent and accept a paid app.
first_notes: Polished native macOS-only equivalent (paid); DevToys is free, MIT, and cross-platform.

first_choose_when: Choose Diffusers when you need a Python library, not a GUI.
first_notes: Python library for scripting diffusion pipelines programmatically; no GUI, intended for developers building their own tools.

first_choose_when: macOS-native desktop app for Stable Diffusion.
first_notes: No command-line or extension ecosystem; Apple Silicon optimized but platform-locked.

first_choose_when: Choose direct-to-S3 when upload bytes can bypass your servers entirely.
first_notes: Best scalability and durability, but pushes object-storage and client-upload logic into the product.

first_choose_when: Use Windows native frameworks for Windows-only media apps.
first_notes: Windows-native; GStreamer is cross-platform but not the idiomatic Windows choice.

first_choose_when: Choose Distroless when you can rebuild on minimal base images instead of shrinking an existing image.
first_notes: Minimal base images you *build on* — deterministic, no runtime tracing, but you must restructure the Dockerfile (multi-stage) and own the source. SlimToolkit retrofits an already-built image instead.

first_choose_when: Choose Django built-in permissions for model-level, DB-backed, admin-managed roles; choose django-rules when the missing piece is per-object logic without extra storage.
first_notes: Model-level, DB-backed, admin-managed; no per-object granularity without extra work — django-rules fills exactly that gap.

first_choose_when: Choose django-allauth for Django apps that want social and local auth wired into Django's user/session model; choose Authomatic when framework-agnostic embedding matters more than Django batteries.
first_notes: Django-specific social + local auth integrated with Django's user/session model; batteries-included on Django, not framework-agnostic.

first_choose_when: Choose django-guardian when object grants are data that admins or APIs assign and revoke; choose django-rules when permissions are derived from code predicates and you want no permission tables.
first_notes: Stores per-object permissions as DB rows (assignable via admin/API); the right tool when grants are *data*, but adds tables, queries and sync — heavier than rules-as-logic.

first_choose_when: Choose django-simple-captcha when you need a Django-integrated CAPTCHA field with storage and verification wired in.
first_notes: Less flexible outside Django and heavier than a pure renderer.

first_choose_when: Pick these sibling bpmn.io libraries when the notation is DMN decision tables or forms rather than BPMN process models.
first_notes: Sibling libraries for DMN decision tables and forms; same team and architecture, but different notations — complementary, not substitutes.

first_choose_when: Choose layer flattening when you only need fewer layers, not content-level minimization.
first_notes: Reduces layer count/dup, not the *contents* — keeps every unused binary. Different mechanism, far smaller win.

first_choose_when: Treat DockerSlim as the predecessor/name history, not a separate current project choice.
first_notes: Not a separate project — DockerSlim was renamed to Slim/SlimToolkit; the same codebase, same `slim build` flow. [推断]

first_choose_when: Choose Docspell for an email-first inbox and metadata-extraction workflow; keep paperless-ngx when a Docker-first scanned-paper archive and the larger self-hosted DMS community matter more.
first_notes: Inbox/metadata-extraction model with strong email ingestion; Scala/JVM stack means heavier memory footprint and a smaller community than paperless-ngx.

first_choose_when: Choose docTR for a clean Python deep-learning detection-plus-recognition pipeline on varied layouts; choose Tesseract for lighter dependencies, broad language data, and stable offline CLI/library use.
first_notes: Deep-learning OCR (detection + recognition) in TF/PyTorch with a clean Python API; better on varied layouts than Tesseract, heavier deps, smaller language coverage.

first_choose_when: Choose raw Dolt when you want versioned SQL but will build the issue schema and agent ergonomics yourself.
first_notes: Same versioned-SQL superpowers without an opinionated schema, but you build the issue schema, dependency logic, ready-detection and agent ergonomics yourself — beads is that opinionated layer.

first_choose_when: Choose hand-rolled dotfiles when you need full control and a minimal surface you maintain yourself.
first_notes: Full control and minimal surface; you maintain every skill/hook/rule yourself instead of inheriting and updating a curated stack.

first_choose_when: Choose Dragonfly when you need a modern high-throughput Redis-compatible store.
first_notes: Modern multithreaded Redis-compatible store; very high throughput but in-memory-first, BSL-licensed — different licensing and capacity model.

first_choose_when: Choose Dramatiq when you want a modern Python task queue with RabbitMQ/Redis support and fewer Celery-era foot-guns.
first_notes: Smaller ecosystem and fewer canvas/workflow primitives than Celery.

first_choose_when: Use Excalidraw for lightweight, hand-drawn sketch whiteboarding; choose draw.io when you need a full WYSIWYG canvas with rich shapes and integrations.
first_notes: Full-featured WYSIWYG canvas editor with Google Drive / OneDrive / GitHub integrations; heavier and more formal than Excalidraw's sketch style.

first_choose_when: Choose DrissionPage when you need a modern Chinese-ecosystem browser-automation/scraping library.
first_notes: Modern Chinese-ecosystem browser-automation/scraping lib; a living alternative for the same "log in to a CN site then scrape" goal.

first_choose_when: Choose DSSIM when you need a standalone structural dissimilarity metric.
first_notes: Structural dissimilarity metric based on SSIM; simpler and older than SSIMULACRA2's multiscale XYB approach.

first_choose_when: Choose E2B when you need a popular hosted-plus-OSS sandbox SDK for agent code execution.
first_notes: Popular hosted+OSS sandbox SDK for agent code execution; managed cloud is turnkey, but self-hosting and multi-runtime breadth differ — OpenSandbox foregrounds K8s-scale + multiple secure runtimes.

first_choose_when: Choose E2B or Daytona when you need code-execution sandboxes for agents.
first_notes: Code-execution sandboxes for agents — overlap on VM isolation, but oriented at running code, not screenshot-driving a GUI desktop.

project_or_alternative: Each agent's built-in skills / slash commands
first_choose_when: Pick native skills when you want the platform-owned command ecosystem instead of a third-party bundle.
first_notes: The platform's own skill ecosystem; this is a third-party bundle layered on top, so it can duplicate or conflict with native skills.

first_choose_when: Choose EasyOCR when a Python/PyTorch OCR stack with good scene-text defaults is easier than image preprocessing; choose Tesseract for mature C++ CPU throughput and long-lived document pipelines.
first_notes: PyTorch-based, 80+ languages, easy install, good on scene/photo text out of the box; bigger runtime and GPU-friendly, less battle-tested at extreme scale than Tesseract's C++ core.

first_choose_when: Choose Elastic-Job when Java distributed scheduling with strong **sharding** and ZooKeeper coordination is the hard requirement.
first_notes: Decentralized, but heavier infra dependency and steeper setup than XXL-JOB's DB-backed admin.

first_choose_when: The incumbent desktop web framework.
first_notes: Electron bundles Chromium, resulting in large binaries and high memory use; Tauri uses the OS webview and is far lighter.

first_choose_when: Choose the old Python Open Interpreter when you need the original natural-language computer REPL.
first_notes: The **original** Python "natural-language interface for computers" REPL, now community-maintained. Choose this if you actually wanted the legacy Python tool; expect community-pace maintenance.

first_choose_when: Choose Envoy when you need an xDS data plane or service-mesh proxy; choose Kong when you want turnkey API-management and AI-gateway plugins rather than building a control plane.
first_notes: CNCF-graduated C++ L4/L7 proxy and the de-facto service-mesh data plane (xDS); far lower-level — you bring a control plane, not turnkey API-management plugins.

first_choose_when: Choose Envoy filters when the proxy platform itself should be Envoy with xDS, observability, and Lua/Wasm extension points.
first_notes: Richer control-plane story, but heavier to operate than NGINX+Lua.

first_choose_when: Choose ESLint/a11y plugins when you need mature AST-based accessibility/code linting.
first_notes: Mature, AST-based linting for accessibility/code, fully offline; but no notion of "AI-design slop" patterns or aesthetic critique, and no agent-skill layer.

first_choose_when: Choose the official React lint rules for canonical hooks coverage with the smallest conceptual surface; choose React Doctor when the agent-skill workflow and extra agent-error rules are the value.
first_notes: The canonical React lint rules; React Doctor overlaps but adds an agent-skill workflow, an oxlint plugin, and curated agent-error rules beyond the official sets.

first_choose_when: Choose ESPnet when you need end-to-end speech processing with deep ASR/TTS recipe coverage and research lineage.
first_notes: Powerful, but historically steeper and more Kaldi-flavored than SpeechBrain.

first_choose_when: Choose EVA-CLIP when you need scaled CLIP with an improved training recipe and larger backbones.
first_notes: Scaled CLIP with improved training recipe and larger backbones; higher accuracy ceiling, heavier weights and compute.

first_choose_when: Choose search backends when you need semantic, agent-search, or self-hosted meta-search.
first_notes: Search backends (semantic / agent-search / self-hosted meta-search). Agent-Reach actually wraps Exa via MCP; these give you search but not the per-platform social-scrape stack.

first_choose_when: Pick Fabric when you need high-level remote task orchestration built on Paramiko.
first_notes: High-level remote-execution framework built *on* Paramiko; great for task orchestration, but it's a layer above, not a transport library.

first_choose_when: Use Ray Serve when you need distributed autoscaling, multi-model composition, and production-grade serving; choose FastAPI when you want a minimal, lightweight API framework for simple serving.
first_notes: Minimal, lightweight API framework; not model-serving-specific, no built-in autoscaling or distributed execution.

first_choose_when: Use Whisper when you need the reference implementation or the latest model weights; choose faster-whisper when you need 2-4x speedup via CTranslate2 and quantized inference on CPU/GPU.
first_notes: A community reimplementation using CTranslate2 and FasterTransformer. Significantly faster, same model weights, but lags behind OpenAI releases and is a downstream project, not the source of truth.

first_choose_when: Choose Feedly or Inoreader when hosted cross-platform discovery, rules, and service features matter; choose NetNewsWire when you want an Apple-native client over a simpler chronological feed list.
first_notes: Hosted SaaS readers with discovery and rules; cross-platform and feature-rich but proprietary and data-hungry — NetNewsWire can act as a native client to some of these.

first_choose_when: Choose Fiddler when Windows-first debugging proxy heritage and .NET scripting matter.
first_notes: Long-standing Windows-first debugging proxy (Fiddler Classic / Everywhere); rich .NET ecosystem and FiddlerScript, but heavier and partly commercial/closed.

first_choose_when: Choose figlet / toilet when you need the classic C banner generators from shell scripts.
first_notes: The classic C banner generators; require a system binary and aren't a Python API — fine for shell use, awkward to embed.

first_choose_when: Use Excalidraw for quick, informal sketch whiteboarding; choose Figma when you need high-fidelity UI design, prototyping, and design-system management.
first_notes: Industry-standard design tool for UI/UX; not a sketch whiteboard, requires a paid team plan for full features.

first_choose_when: Choose Figma plus plugins when you need full manual design control and collaboration.
first_notes: Full design control and collaboration, but manual; no agent-driven 7-step flow, no auto image sourcing, and not a repo you can vendor.

first_choose_when: Pick Figma or Penpot when you need multiplayer vector editing, not generated code-rendered artifacts.
first_notes: True vector design editors with multiplayer; Open Design generates code-rendered artifacts, not editable vector docs.

first_choose_when: Choose Filebrowser when a simpler Go single-binary web file manager is enough; keep copyparty when resumable accelerated uploads, protocol breadth, or the media indexer are the deciding features.
first_notes: Comparable lightweight single-binary web file manager (Go). Narrower protocol set and no `up2k`-style resumable accelerated uploads or media indexer; simpler to reason about.

first_choose_when: Choose fine-tuning or LoRA stacks when you need to change weights to improve a capability.
first_notes: Change weights to improve a capability; this is orthogonal (no training) and the author notes you can stack both. Different cost/benefit and reproducibility profile.

first_choose_when: Google's managed backend-as-a-service (BaaS).
first_notes: Firebase is fully managed and has a broader mobile SDK ecosystem, but it locks you into proprietary NoSQL (Firestore) and Google's platform. Supabase gives you open-source Postgres and avoids vendor lock-in.

first_choose_when: Choose Flink CDC when you need full stream-processing CDC with transforms and many connectors.
first_notes: Full stream-processing CDC with transforms and many connectors; powerful and maintained, far heavier operationally.

first_choose_when: Pick Flowise when you want a similar visual LLM builder and its ecosystem fits your stack better.
first_notes: Very similar feature set; Langflow has a larger community and more active GitHub presence as of 2026-07.

first_choose_when: Choose Fluent Bit or Fluentd when logs and events are the primary payload.
first_notes: Log-and-event shippers first (Fluent Bit is also a tiny C binary); narrower metrics surface than Telegraf's 300+ plugins.

first_choose_when: Google's cross-platform UI framework with native rendering.
first_notes: Flutter requires learning Dart and its widget system; Tauri reuses web skills but is less native-feeling on desktop.

first_choose_when: Choose FontForge when you need a full GUI/scriptable font editor for design and production.
first_notes: Full GUI/scriptable font editor (design + production); much broader feature surface but heavier, C-based, and a different (editor) workflow than a clean Python library.

first_choose_when: Choose Fooocus when you want a minimal local prompt-to-image experience.
first_notes: Minimal prompt-to-image UI inspired by Midjourney; great for quick results but far less flexible than ComfyUI's node graph.

first_choose_when: Choose FreeType when you need a C rasterizer/loader for rendering glyphs at runtime.
first_notes: C rasterizer/loader for rendering glyphs at runtime; about drawing pixels, not editing font files.

first_choose_when: Choose FreshRSS when you need the self-hosted feed server and web UI; choose NetNewsWire as the native Apple client that can sit on top of that backend.
first_notes: Self-hosted PHP feed *server* + web UI; you run it, it syncs to many clients (including NetNewsWire) — a backend, not a native client.

first_choose_when: Choose FriendlyCaptcha when you want privacy-focused PoW but are comfortable with the maintained product being hosted and commercial.
first_notes: Cap is fully open-source and self-hosted instead.

first_choose_when: Choose gallery-dl when you need a broad multi-site media downloader that includes Reddit.
first_notes: Broad multi-site media downloader (Reddit among many); strong for *files* across the web, but weaker at Reddit-specific metadata/comment archiving and the three-mode download/archive/clone model.

first_choose_when: Choose Gamma or Tome when hosted AI deck SaaS is acceptable.
first_notes: Hosted AI deck SaaS, not a repo — easier for non-agents, but closed, no single-file HTML artifact, no local agent control.

first_choose_when: Choose Garak when the task is dedicated Python red-team scanning only; choose promptfoo when red-team checks must sit beside general eval assertions in one workflow.
first_notes: Dedicated LLM vulnerability scanner (red-team only, Python). Overlaps promptfoo's `redteam` scope but isn't a general eval/assertion harness.

first_choose_when: Choose gateway-native plugins when you want rate-limit/cache product features instead of a raw Redis driver.
first_notes: Higher-level feature layer; often uses this kind of driver underneath.

first_choose_when: Choose GDAL/OGR for scripted ETL, conversion, and CI-friendly code paths; choose QGIS for interactive desktop mapping, project authoring, and visual analysis.
first_notes: The underlying I/O + raster/vector translation library QGIS itself depends on; a CLI/library, not a desktop app — choose it for scripted ETL, not interactive mapping.

first_choose_when: Choose ad-hoc prompts only when you do not need a curated framework or persistent author voice.
first_notes: Ad-hoc prompts have no curated framework, case library, or persistence; dbskill ships ~4k knowledge atoms and state commands behind a coherent author voice.

first_choose_when: Choose the original Ralph loop when you only need the raw one-line shell technique.
first_notes: The raw technique is a one-line shell loop; this project is that idea plus exit gating, rate limits, circuit breaker, monitoring, backups, and sandboxing — i.e. the safety scaffolding the bare loop lacks.

first_choose_when: Choose GeoPandas and Shapely for Python-native reproducible vector pipelines; choose QGIS when GUI editing, cartographic layouts, or raster-first workflows matter.
first_notes: Python-native vector analysis for code-first/reproducible pipelines; no GUI, no cartographic print layout, no raster-first workflow.

first_choose_when: Choose GeoServer when the requirement is an OGC publishing server; choose QGIS when you need desktop authoring/analysis or QGIS Server tied to QGIS projects.
first_notes: Java OGC server focused on publishing (WMS/WFS/WCS); overlaps QGIS Server on the publishing side but has no desktop authoring/analysis GUI.

first_choose_when: Choose Gerapy when you need a Django + Vue dashboard for distributed Scrapy management.
first_notes: Django + Vue dashboard for distributed Scrapy management; more modern and generally the recommended successor in this niche today.

first_choose_when: Choose Giskard for broader ML+LLM testing with a Python-centric scan/report model; choose promptfoo when prompt and CI regression workflows are the center.
first_notes: OSS testing/red-teaming for ML+LLM with a scan-and-report model; broader ML scope, Python-centric. promptfoo is more prompt/CI-workflow focused.

first_choose_when: Search within tracked files using git's own index.
first_notes: git grep is fast for tracked files but only works inside Git repos; ripgrep works anywhere and searches untracked files too.

first_choose_when: Choose git submodules or manual copying when zero new dependency and transparency matter most.
first_notes: Zero new dependency and fully transparent, but no cross-agent path resolution, no discovery registry, no bulk `update` — the manual flow Skills replaces.

first_choose_when: Pick roll-your-own AST scripts when control matters more than bundled query, clustering, visualization, and agent integration.
first_notes: Roll-your-own AST graphs; more control, but you build query, clustering, viz, and agent integration yourself.

first_choose_when: Choose GitHub Actions plus an agent CLI when you want roll-your-own issue-triggered agent runs.
first_notes: Roll-your-own: CI triggers an agent on issues. More control and durable infra (CI runners), but you build the dispatch/reconciliation/isolation that Symphony gives you.

first_choose_when: Choose hosted CI when VCS-tied YAML pipelines matter more than self-hosting a pipeline server.
first_notes: Hosted, YAML-driven CI/CD tied to your VCS; far lower setup friction than self-hosting a pipeline server.

first_choose_when: Choose CodeQL when native GitHub code scanning and deep dataflow/taint analysis are required; choose this tool when you want Claude-written line comments and remediation prose on changed files.
first_notes: Deep dataflow/taint analysis, native code-scanning UI, free for public repos; per-language, heavier setup, no LLM remediation prose.

first_choose_when: AI pair programmer IDE extension.
first_notes: Copilot is IDE-integrated and subscription-based; Codex is terminal-first and standalone with shell execution.

first_choose_when: AI-powered CLI from GitHub/Microsoft.
first_notes: Copilot CLI is Copilot-subscription based and IDE-integrated; Gemini CLI is standalone and free-tier accessible.

first_choose_when: Choose GitHub Issues when you need a mature hosted tracker with web UI and notifications.
first_notes: Mature hosted tracker with web UI/notifications/cross-repo views, but online-first, not branch-scoped/version-controlled, no native dependency-graph + auto-ready for agents.

first_choose_when: Choose GitHub Issues by hand when you want the same backend without CCPM's spec discipline.
first_notes: The same backend CCPM drives, without the opinionated PRD→epic→task decomposition, worktree setup, or bash status scripts — you'd hand-roll the spec discipline and parallel conventions yourself.

first_choose_when: Choose glow when you need a Go single-binary Markdown renderer with a TUI browser/pager and themes.
first_notes: Go single-binary Markdown renderer with a TUI browser/pager and themes (Charm); actively maintained, no Python runtime — generally the modern default for terminal Markdown reading.

first_choose_when: Choose GluonTS when you need a probabilistic time-series toolkit from AWS.
first_notes: Probabilistic time-series toolkit (AWS); strong for real forecasting at scale, steeper learning curve, not an intro example.

first_choose_when: Choose Glyphs or RoboFont when you need commercial macOS type-design apps.
first_notes: Commercial macOS type-design apps; for drawing typefaces, often *use* fontTools under the hood for export.

first_choose_when: Choose Go Playground or `go run` for quick one-off snippets with no need for persistent notebook state.
first_notes: Fine for a snippet, not for prose-plus-code documents or cross-cell state.

first_choose_when: Choose go-mysql directly when you want to build a custom Go syncer.
first_notes: The underlying binlog/replication library this tool is built on; use it directly if you want to build a custom syncer rather than this canned one.

first_choose_when: Choose Godot when you need an actual engine with editor, scenes, 2D/3D, and asset workflow; choose pygame for small Python-first 2D projects and teaching loops.
first_notes: A full open-source game *engine* (editor, scenes, 2D+3D, GDScript/C#); vastly more capable but a whole different tool to learn — overkill for "draw a rect and move it."

first_choose_when: Pick a generic diagramming canvas only when you are prepared to implement BPMN correctness yourself.
first_notes: General commercial/open diagramming canvases you'd build BPMN on top of yourself; more generic, but you implement BPMN correctness, which bpmn-js gives for free.

first_choose_when: Choose Goldmark when you need a fast, extensible Markdown parser in Go.
first_notes: A fast, extensible CommonMark/GFM parser written in Go; not for JS projects.

first_choose_when: Choose gomacro when terminal-based interactive Go is enough and a notebook UI would add overhead.
