first_notes: It is the interpreter lineage gophernotes builds on, but not a Jupyter kernel experience by itself.

first_choose_when: Choose cloud OCR when messy-input accuracy, tables, forms, and managed operations outweigh per-page cost and data residency; choose Tesseract when offline self-hosting is non-negotiable.
first_notes: Managed cloud OCR; best-in-class accuracy on messy input plus Textract's table/form extraction, but per-page cost, data leaves your network, and no offline/self-host — the opposite of Tesseract's deployment model.

first_choose_when: The incumbent cloud photo service with unlimited storage (for compressed) and best-in-class ML search.
first_notes: Google hosts your data and trains models on it; Immich keeps everything local but you run the hardware.

first_choose_when: Choose managed CAPTCHA services when stronger hosted bot signals matter more than self-hosting.
first_notes: Third-party network calls, privacy/data-sharing concerns, and no self-hosting; stronger signals than a simple generated challenge.

first_choose_when: Choose Goose3 when you need a Python port of the Goose article extractor.
first_notes: Python port of Goose article extractor; same niche as newspaper (text/metadata/top-image), different heuristics — a direct peer to benchmark against.

first_choose_when: Choose GPT Researcher when you need a larger Python feature surface with reports and UI.
first_notes: Python, much larger feature surface (multiple retrievers, report types, web UI); deep-research trades all that breadth for a readable minimal core.

first_choose_when: Choose cloud frontier models when quality and zero deployment effort outweigh offline/device constraints.
first_notes: Frontier multimodal quality and zero deployment effort, but cloud-only — network dependency, per-call cost, no offline/on-device, and your data leaves the device. The opposite tradeoff from MiniCPM-V.

first_choose_when: Choose a VLM when messy screenshots, surrounding context, or rapid model improvement matter more than a lightweight purpose-built local tool; choose pix2tex for offline, small-scope equation crops.
first_notes: General vision-language models that transcribe equations to LaTeX zero-shot; stronger on messy/contextual input and actively improving, but heavier (API cost or large local weights) and not a purpose-built, lightweight equation tool.

first_choose_when: Choose GPT-Researcher when you need a lightweight open agent over LLM APIs and web tools.
first_notes: Lightweight open research agent that orchestrates a frozen LLM API + web tools; far cheaper to run (no self-hosted weights) but not its own fine-tuned models or benchmark-tuned framework.

first_choose_when: Choose Grafana + Prometheus when you need observability dashboards for metrics and alerts across a fleet.
first_notes: Observability dashboards for metrics/alerting across a fleet; read-mostly monitoring, whereas Cockpit is hands-on administration of a single host.

first_choose_when: Choose GraphRAG when you need an LLM-built entity/community graph for document RAG.
first_notes: LLM-built entity/community graph for document RAG; aimed at unstructured corpora, not deterministic AST-derived code graphs.

first_choose_when: Pick Graphviz when mature graph layout algorithms for large or dense graphs matter more than Markdown-native rendering.
first_notes: Mature, scriptable graph **layout** engine with strong algorithms for large/dense graphs; produces excellent auto-layout but DOT is lower-level and not natively rendered inline by docs platforms the way Mermaid is.

first_choose_when: Pick Graphviz/Viz.js when strong automatic layout for arbitrary node-link graphs matters more than flowchart-shaped semantics.
first_notes: DOT language with strong automatic graph layout for arbitrary node-link graphs; better layout engine, less flowchart-shaped semantics and styling.

first_choose_when: Choose GRASS GIS for deep raster analysis and topology-heavy workflows; choose QGIS when desktop cartography, editing, and a friendlier plugin/processing shell matter more.
first_notes: Deep raster/geospatial-analysis engine and topology model; steeper UI, often used *through* QGIS as a Processing provider rather than standalone.

first_choose_when: The standard POSIX search utility, available everywhere.
first_notes: grep is universal and standard but slower and noisier; ripgrep is faster, smarter, and respects gitignore by default.

first_choose_when: Choose grep over local session dirs when zero-dependency local search is enough.
first_notes: Zero-dependency and fully local, but no UI, no token/cost math, no cross-agent normalization.

first_choose_when: Choose gRPC and Protocol Buffers for new RPC designs that do not need Thrift wire compatibility.
first_notes: Larger modern ecosystem over HTTP/2/protobuf, but it is a migration to a different protocol.

first_choose_when: Choose GSAP when plugin breadth, ScrollTrigger/MorphSVG-style features, and commercial support are decisive; choose Anime.js for a smaller MIT, dependency-free, framework-agnostic animator.
first_notes: Larger, more mature ecosystem (ScrollTrigger, MorphSVG, physics plugins) and commercial support; heavier mindshare. Anime.js is smaller, MIT-licensed, dependency-free, and now fully modular in v4.

first_choose_when: Choose Guidance/Guardrails when you only need output constraints for single-call structured generation.
first_notes: Output-constraint / structured-generation libraries (constrain a single LLM call's format/validity); narrower than Parlant's conversation-level behavioral control across a multi-turn dialogue.

first_choose_when: Choose guppy3/heapy for in-process heap analysis, or Scalene for maintained CPU/GPU/memory profiling.
first_notes: Both answer "where is memory going" with maintained tooling, but neither matches memory-analyzer's arbitrary live-PID snapshot niche.

first_choose_when: Choose gVisor, Kata, or Firecracker directly when you only need isolation primitives.
first_notes: The isolation primitives themselves — OpenSandbox orchestrates these; using them directly means building the sandbox lifecycle/API/scheduling yourself.

first_choose_when: Choose hand-rolled scripts only when your schema and deletion policy need full custom control.
first_notes: Full control, exactly your schema; but you write, test, and maintain destructive SQL yourself — this repo is the proven starting point.

project_or_alternative: Hand-rolled context/memory skills in your own repo
first_choose_when: Choose custom skills when maximum fit and zero lock-in outweigh a ready-made corpus.
first_notes: Maximum fit and zero lock-in, but you author and maintain everything. This pack trades some fit for a ready-made, benchmarked corpus.

first_choose_when: Choose hand-rolled parsing only when you need no dependency and accept reimplementing HLS grammar.
first_notes: No dependency, but you reimplement the tag grammar, variant/media structure, and serialization — and HLS has many edge cases this library already handles.

first_choose_when: Choose custom subagents/skills when maximum fit and zero stack conflict outweigh ready-made breadth.
first_notes: Maximum fit and zero conflict with your existing stack, but you author and maintain everything. This repo trades bespoke fit for ready-made breadth you must still vet.

first_choose_when: Choose a hand-written prompt when a few maintained inline rules are enough.
first_notes: A few inline rules you maintain yourself: zero install and fully yours, but you re-derive and re-tune the pattern list instead of inheriting a vetted ~24-item checklist.

project_or_alternative: Hand-written design checklist in your own `CLAUDE.md` / prompt
first_choose_when: Choose a hand-written checklist when you want zero third-party skill dependency.
first_notes: The DIY alternative; same advisory nature, but you maintain it. This skill packages a known-good detail list so you don't re-derive it per project.

first_choose_when: Pick a hand-written `DESIGN.md` when you need a bespoke per-project design contract you maintain.
first_notes: A bespoke per-project design contract you maintain; more tailored and stable, but you build and enforce it yourself instead of getting a 161-rule starter.

first_choose_when: Choose hand-written skills when full control and zero third-party surface matter most.
first_notes: Writing your own `SKILL.md` for translate/format gives full control and zero third-party surface, but you rebuild and maintain the three-mode workflow, glossary handling, and HTML theming yourself.

first_choose_when: Choose HarfBuzz when you need a text shaping engine rather than a font-file editing library.
first_notes: Text shaping engine (text → positioned glyphs); complementary, not a substitute — fontTools edits the font, HarfBuzz uses it to shape.

first_choose_when: Choose harness-mem when you need the optional cross-session memory add-on.
first_notes: An optional cross-session memory add-on referenced by this project; separate concern (agent memory), not a workflow substitute.

first_choose_when: Auto-generated GraphQL API over Postgres.
first_notes: Hasura is excellent for GraphQL-only APIs but lacks the built-in auth, storage, and edge functions that Supabase bundles.

first_choose_when: Choose Haystack or django-elasticsearch-dsl when you need a higher-level framework/integration layer.
first_notes: Higher-level search framework / Django integration layered on top; more opinionated, narrower than the raw DSL.

first_choose_when: Choose hCaptcha when a managed image-challenge service and publisher-payment ecosystem matter more than self-hosting.
first_notes: Still third-party and image-based. Cap is a much smaller self-hostable widget with no external calls.

first_choose_when: Choose headless Chrome with Puppeteer when you need the standard maintained Chromium replacement.
first_notes: The standard replacement: a maintained, modern Chromium engine driven by a Node.js library over CDP — accurate rendering, active security patching, huge ecosystem; single-engine (Chromium) and Node-centric, but that's the right default for new work.

first_choose_when: Choose Headless UI when you want Tailwind-compatible, unstyled components from the Tailwind team.
first_notes: Tailwind-team-authored unstyled components; fewer primitives than Radix and no built-in "copy to own" distribution system.

first_choose_when: Choose Helicone when logging, cost tracking, caching, and proxy-based adoption are the main needs; keep Pezzo only if its prompt-versioning UI already fits and the stall risk is acceptable.
first_notes: Open-source LLM observability/proxy focused on logging, cost, and caching; lighter to adopt (proxy-based), narrower prompt-management story.

first_choose_when: Choose Heroku 12-Factor App when you need the original SaaS-app methodology this borrows its name/format from.
first_notes: The original SaaS-app methodology this borrows its name/format from; about apps, not agents.

first_choose_when: Pick closed SaaS tools when speed for a single generated clip matters more than pipeline control and OSS extensibility.
first_notes: Faster for a single clip, but no pipeline customization, no agent approval gates, no open-source extensibility, and ongoing subscription costs.

first_choose_when: Choose HF TRL when you need a mature PPO/GRPO/DPO library for dataset- or loop-centric training.
first_notes: No agent-execution decoupling or multi-step credit assignment out of the box.

first_choose_when: Choose hls.js or other-language parsers when you need mature HLS parsing outside Python.
first_notes: Mature HLS parsers in other runtimes (JS, Go); same job, wrong language if you're in Python.

first_choose_when: Choose hnswlib when a tiny HNSW-only C++/Python library is enough.
first_notes: Tiny header-only C++/Python HNSW-only library; even lighter than FAISS and easy to embed, but single-algorithm and no GPU / PQ / clustering breadth.

first_choose_when: Choose httpx for new code that can use a modern sync/async client and wants HTTP/2 support.
first_notes: Better long-term path for concurrent HTTP, but async concurrency requires `async`/`await` rather than drop-in `requests` calls.

first_choose_when: Choose httpx plus BeautifulSoup/parsel when you want the mainstream maintained HTTP-client-plus-parser split.
first_notes: The mainstream modern split: an actively-maintained async-capable HTTP client plus a dedicated parser (bs4 for forgiving HTML, parsel for Scrapy-style CSS/XPath). Two imports instead of one, but both are maintained and you control each piece — the recommended replacement for plain HTML scraping.

first_choose_when: Choose Hugging Face transformers when you want the OpenAI CLIP weights behind a maintained batteries-included API.
first_notes: The same OpenAI weights wrapped in a maintained, batteries-included API (processors, `from_pretrained`, pipelines); easier to integrate and keep current, at the cost of the heavier `transformers` dependency.

first_choose_when: Choose Hugging Face sentiment models when you need a large catalog of fine-tuned models with easy integration.
first_notes: Huge catalog of fine-tuned sentiment models (incl. Chinese) on PyTorch/Transformers with trivial install; not the specific SKEP method, but far easier to adopt and maintain.

first_choose_when: Choose Transformers audio models when using or fine-tuning pretrained Whisper/Wav2Vec2-style models is enough.
first_notes: Excellent model access, but not a full recipe/training framework spanning separation, enhancement, and diarization.

first_choose_when: Choose HuggingGPT/JARVIS when you need the same-era LLM-controller-over-model-catalog idea.
first_notes: Same era, same idea — an LLM controller that routes tasks to a catalog of Hugging Face models; broader (not vision-only) task scope, also a research demo rather than a maintained product.

first_choose_when: Choose imageio-ffmpeg when you need a lightweight shim for reading video frames via FFmpeg in imageio.
first_notes: Lightweight shim for reading video frames via FFmpeg in imageio; simpler but less control than PyAV's direct libav bindings.

first_choose_when: Choose imageio-ffmpeg or fluent-ffmpeg when you need other-language or narrower-scope FFmpeg wrappers.
first_notes: Other-language or narrower-scope FFmpeg wrappers (Node's fluent-ffmpeg, Python imageio shim); similar shell-out model, different ergonomics.

first_choose_when: Deep language-specific IDE for JVM and Android.
first_notes: IntelliJ is heavier and JVM-focused; VS Code is lighter and language-agnostic.

first_choose_when: Choose InvokeAI when you want a polished artist-focused canvas.
first_notes: Polished artist-focused canvas with generation and editing in one view; smoother UX but less open/customizable than ComfyUI.

first_choose_when: Choose It-Tools when you need a self-hostable web app with a similar grab-bag of dev utilities.
first_notes: Self-hostable web app with a very similar grab-bag of dev utilities; runs in any browser / Docker. DevToys is native desktop + offline + a CLI; It-Tools is zero-install over HTTP.

first_choose_when: Choose itchat-uos when a fragile UOS endpoint patch is the experiment you want.
first_notes: Fork patched against the "UOS" web-WeChat endpoint to coax logins past some of the blocks; buys partial, fragile functionality on some accounts but is itself lightly maintained and fights the same platform that keeps closing the door.

first_choose_when: Use Alacritty for cross-platform, minimal GPU terminal emulation; choose iTerm2 when you want the most popular macOS terminal with deep macOS integration and extensive features.
first_notes: iTerm2 is macOS-only and feature-rich; Alacritty is cross-platform and minimal.

first_choose_when: Use JACK/PulseAudio for Linux desktop audio routing and pro-audio low-latency.
first_notes: Audio servers, not video pipelines. GStreamer can use them as sinks but is a higher-level processing framework.

first_choose_when: Choose the Java/Scala client for JVM services, reference-client behavior, or Kafka Streams; choose kafka-python when the application boundary is Python and a JVM client is not acceptable.
first_notes: The reference implementation with first-class feature support and Kafka Streams, but JVM-only — not an option for a Python service.

first_choose_when: Pick engine-bundled modelers when tight coupling to a Java process engine is the point.
first_notes: Engine-bundled BPMN modelers tied to a specific Java process engine; integrated execution but heavier and less embeddable as a standalone JS canvas.

first_choose_when: Choose Jenkins when the problem is CI/CD with a vast plugin ecosystem rather than general-purpose Gaia-style workflow plugins.
first_notes: Old but still-maintained CI/CD server with vast plugin ecosystem; Groovy/declarative pipelines instead of compiled-code plugins.

first_choose_when: Choose the JetBrains stock keymap when you need a fully supported setup with no emulation layer.
first_notes: No emulation layer, fully supported; but no Vim modes/motions — defeats the purpose for a Vim user.

first_choose_when: Choose jMetal when you need an established multi-objective metaheuristics framework in the Java/Python ecosystem.
first_notes: Established multi-objective metaheuristics framework; jMetalPy mirrors it in Python — comparable goals, different ecosystem and API style.

first_choose_when: Choose jp2a when you need a fast C CLI that converts JPEG/PNG to coloured ASCII.
first_notes: Fast C CLI converting JPEG/PNG to ASCII with colour; a single binary, mature, but not a Python API.

first_choose_when: Pick these when the real constraint is Java or JavaScript runtime rather than Python.
first_notes: Reddit API wrappers for other languages (Java / JS); same niche, different runtime.

first_choose_when: Choose Jupyter Kernel Gateway or nsjail when you need narrower code-execution/isolation tools.
first_notes: Narrower, single-purpose code-execution/isolation tools; less of an agent-oriented platform.

first_choose_when: Choose another Jupyter language kernel when the actual need is Rust, JavaScript, or another language inside notebooks.
first_notes: Same pattern as gophernotes, but maintenance and completeness vary per language.

first_choose_when: Choose kafbat/kafka-ui for new deployments or upgrades because it is the maintained continuation; use this page mainly to understand the stalled Provectus upstream and migration risk.
first_notes: The **maintained community fork** of this exact project — same UI, ongoing releases; for new installs it's generally the better choice than the stalled upstream.

first_choose_when: Choose Kafka KRaft or etcd when the strategic answer is removing ZooKeeper from the stack.
first_notes: The strategic alternative: remove ZooKeeper from your stack entirely, making a ZK GUI moot.

first_choose_when: Treat kafka-python admin CLI as complementary: use it for scriptable or headless admin, and kafka-ui for human browsing and team dashboards.
first_notes: CLI, not a UI — scriptable/headless admin; complements rather than replaces a dashboard.

first_choose_when: Choose Kaldi when you need the classic, highly optimized ASR toolkit and accept C++/shell-heavy workflows.
first_notes: Maximizes control, not ergonomics; it is far steeper and not PyTorch-native.

first_choose_when: Kdenlive is built on MLT. Use Kdenlive when you want a KDE-integrated NLE; use MLT directly when you need the engine.
first_notes: Another open-source NLE built on MLT; KDE/Qt integration, more features than Shotcut in some areas, but still an app, not a library.

first_choose_when: Use Vaultwarden for self-hosted server-based password management with official Bitwarden clients; choose KeePassXC when you want an offline, local-first password database with no server at all.
first_notes: No server to run, but no native sync, no web vault, and no official mobile clients — a different architecture entirely.

first_choose_when: Choose Keras official tutorials when you need current maintained TF2 examples of the same techniques.
first_notes: Up-to-date, maintained, TF2 examples of the same techniques; less narrative than the companion article but won't bit-rot the same way.

first_choose_when: Choose Keycloak or Auth0 when you need an identity platform with SSO, MFA, admin, or SAML; choose Authomatic only for app-embedded OAuth/OpenID login client duties.
first_notes: Full identity providers (hosted or self-run) — SSO, MFA, admin, SAML; a platform, not a client library — different scope entirely.

first_choose_when: Choose KeyDB when you need a multithreaded Redis fork that stays memory-resident.
first_notes: Multithreaded Redis fork, still memory-resident; helps throughput, not the capacity-vs-RAM-cost problem PikiwiDB targets.

first_choose_when: Pick Kibana when the stack is deliberately Elasticsearch/OpenSearch-centered.
first_notes: Tightly coupled to Elasticsearch/OpenSearch; superb for log search and the Elastic stack, but narrower as a multi-backend dashboarding tool than Grafana's data-source-agnostic model.

first_choose_when: Use Alacritty for minimal, raw-performance GPU terminal emulation; choose Kitty when you want a GPU-based terminal with advanced features like kittens (plugins) and image support.
first_notes: Kitty has more features and a plugin system; Alacritty is simpler and more focused on raw performance.

first_choose_when: Choose KrakenD for stateless API aggregation from a single config file; choose Kong when the edge needs a plugin ecosystem, admin API, and richer runtime policy.
first_notes: Stateless Go gateway focused on API aggregation/composition declared in one config file; no database, but not a plugin-rich programmable edge.

first_choose_when: Choose Krita with AI Diffusion when you need a full painting app with an SD plugin.
first_notes: Full painting app with an SD plugin and live generation inside a real art tool; far richer canvas, heavier setup, more actively developed.

first_choose_when: Use Ray Serve when you want a Python-first, code-centric serving framework; choose KServe when you need Kubernetes-native model serving with standard CRDs and tight Kubeflow integration.
first_notes: Kubernetes-native model serving with standard CRDs and tight Kubeflow integration; more YAML/config-heavy, less Python-native than Ray Serve.

first_choose_when: Choose Kvrocks when you need a RocksDB-backed Redis-protocol Apache project.
first_notes: RocksDB-backed, Redis-protocol, now an Apache project; the closest direct competitor — weigh Apache governance vs PikiwiDB's OpenAtom/Qihoo backing.

first_choose_when: Choose LangChain agents when you need a maintained general-purpose LLM tool-orchestration framework.
first_notes: Maintained, general-purpose LLM tool-orchestration framework; you wire your own tools (including vision models) with current function-calling, instead of TaskMatrix's hand-rolled 2023 prompt-router.

first_choose_when: Choose Langfuse for new open-source LLM observability, prompt management, and eval deployments; keep Pezzo only for an existing self-hosted Pezzo stack you are prepared to maintain yourself.
first_notes: Open-source LLM observability + prompt management + evals, actively maintained with a strong community; broadly the healthier successor to Pezzo's niche today.

first_choose_when: Choose Langfuse or Helicone when you need production LLM observability platforms.
first_notes: Production LLM observability platforms (tracing, evals); built for app pipelines and usually hosted/instrumented, not local-first browsing of *your own* coding-agent sessions.

first_choose_when: Choose LangGraph when you need graph/state-machine orchestration with a large ecosystem and explicit control flow.
first_notes: Graph/state-machine orchestration with a large ecosystem and explicit control flow; heavier, more opinionated than AgentScope's "trust the model" loop.

first_choose_when: Choose LangMem when your memory layer should stay inside LangChain/LangGraph.
first_notes: Memory utilities tied to the LangChain/LangGraph ecosystem; Mem0 is framework-neutral.

first_choose_when: Choose LangSmith for hosted LangChain-centric evals and observability; choose promptfoo when OSS, local-first execution, and framework-agnostic providers are hard requirements.
first_notes: Hosted LangChain eval/observability SaaS; deep LangChain integration and managed dashboards, but proprietary and cloud-centric. promptfoo is OSS, local-first, framework-agnostic.

first_choose_when: Choose LangSmith when managed tracing, evals, prompt hub, and LangChain integration matter more than self-hosted OSS; keep Pezzo only when SaaS is off the table and self-maintenance is acceptable.
first_notes: Hosted tracing + evals + prompt hub, deep LangChain integration; managed and feature-rich, but proprietary/SaaS, not self-hostable OSS.

first_choose_when: Choose LaunchBar when you want a long-standing supported keyboard launcher as a separate app.
first_notes: Long-standing keyboard launcher; mature and supported, separate app, not a Spotlight plugin layer.

first_choose_when: Pick lego when you need a static Go binary or embeddable Go ACME library with broad DNS support.
first_notes: Single static Go binary, ACME client + Go library, broad DNS provider support; great for embedding/automation, but no web-server config installer.

first_choose_when: Choose Letta when you want a stateful runtime to own the agent loop and memory OS.
first_notes: Stateful agent runtime with a self-editing memory OS and a server; owns the agent loop. claude-mem slots under your existing agents via hooks rather than replacing them.

first_choose_when: Choose Letta Code when you want the team's full coding-agent product instead of this demo.
first_notes: The production sibling from the same team — a full coding agent on the Letta platform. The README explicitly recommends it over this demo for real use.

first_choose_when: Only choose libav when you are maintaining legacy systems that still ship `avconv`.
first_notes: Historical 2011 fork of FFmpeg; merged back into irrelevance and effectively dead. Old distros shipped `avconv`; for any new work use FFmpeg, not libav.

first_choose_when: Choose LibreChat when you need a full multi-user platform rather than a lightweight single-deploy client.
first_notes: Accounts, many auth backends, RAG, assistants, and code interpreter; far more capable and far heavier to run. NextChat is a lighter client, not a team platform.

first_choose_when: Lightweight self-hosted photo manager with face recognition.
first_notes: LibrePhotos is lighter on resources but has a smaller community and less polished mobile experience.

first_choose_when: Pick libssh2 bindings when transfer speed and a C-backed dependency matter more than Pythonic ergonomics.
first_notes: C library bindings — faster transfers, but a compiled dependency and a thinner Pythonic API.

first_choose_when: Choose Lighthouse or axe-core when you need rendered-page performance/accessibility audits.
first_notes: Audits performance/accessibility on rendered pages; overlaps on URL scanning but not on AI-design-pattern detection or the skill-driven "polish/bolder/quieter" workflow.

first_choose_when: Pick measurement tools when you need real metrics, CI budgets, and build-blocking gates.
first_notes: Real measurement + CI gating tools (not skill packs). Use these when you need numbers and build-blocking budgets; this pack is the advisory layer that interprets and fixes, not the meter.

first_choose_when: Choose Linear or Jira when you need a best-in-class human-team tracker.
first_notes: Best-in-class for human teams (workflows, dashboards, guarantees), but heavyweight, online-only, not version-controlled with the code, not agent-native.

first_choose_when: Choose hand-written `tc` plus `fq_codel` when current qdiscs and correctness matter more than wrapper convenience.
first_notes: Same engine with less abstraction, but more configuration to write.

first_choose_when: Choose a purpose-built LLM proxy when all traffic is provider routing and model policy; choose Kong when LLM routing must share one gateway with broader HTTP/API policy.
first_notes: Purpose-built LLM routers focused only on multi-provider LLM traffic; narrower than Kong's combined HTTP + AI gateway, but lighter if LLM routing is all you need.

first_choose_when: Choose llama.cpp when you need a portable C/C++ GGUF engine that runs broadly, including Macs via Metal.
first_notes: The portable C/C++ inference engine (GGUF) running everywhere incl. Macs via Metal; maximally portable and mature, but not MLX-native and no built-in macOS menu-bar/admin management layer.

first_choose_when: Pick LlamaIndex when RAG/data connectors and indices are the core need.
first_notes: RAG/data-framework heavyweight with rich connectors and indices; DSPy is lighter on data plumbing but optimizes the reasoning program itself.

first_choose_when: Full RAG with embeddings and retrieval.
first_notes: RAG pipelines offer dynamic retrieval and semantic search but require more infrastructure; book-to-skill is simpler, static skill generation.

first_choose_when: Pick LlamaParse when a hosted parser for complex PDFs/tables is acceptable despite SaaS pricing and data-boundary tradeoffs.
first_notes: Hosted parsing service (LlamaIndex) strong on complex PDFs/tables; SaaS with usage pricing and data leaving your boundary, vs Docling running fully local/in-process.

first_choose_when: Choose LLaVA when you need the influential open VLM recipe/lineage.
first_notes: The influential open VLM recipe/lineage; great for research and fine-tuning, but generally larger / less optimized for edge deployment out of the box.

first_choose_when: Choose LM Studio when you need a polished desktop app with an OpenAI-compatible server.
first_notes: Polished desktop app for local models on Mac/Win/Linux with an OpenAI-compatible server; closed-source GUI, not an Apple-MLX-native open-source server.

first_choose_when: Choose lm-evaluation-harness when you only need the standard benchmark runner.
first_notes: The standard benchmark runner this repo calls out to for validation; it measures models but doesn't perform or search layer surgery.

first_choose_when: Choose Lobe Chat when you want a polished multi-provider UI with plugins, knowledge base, and optional multi-user modes.
first_notes: Broader feature surface and heavier once cloud/DB features are enabled. NextChat stays minimal and browser-local.

project_or_alternative: Local RAG stacks (LlamaIndex / LangChain retrievers, etc.)
first_choose_when: Choose local RAG when you need self-hosted embeddings and vector storage end-to-end.
first_notes: Self-hosted embeddings + vector DB you own end-to-end; higher setup cost (chunking, embeddings, infra) but no third-party account, no public-share requirement, no browser automation. This skill trades that control for NotebookLM's pre-built Gemini grounding.

first_choose_when: Choose Logstash JDBC input when polling is acceptable and simpler startup matters more than true CDC.
first_notes: Polling-based (not binlog CDC), simpler to start, but query-polling misses deletes and adds DB load; coarser than true CDC.

first_choose_when: Choose Looker when governed semantic modeling in LookML is the core requirement; choose Superset when a lighter self-hosted SQL BI layer is enough.
first_notes: Proprietary (Google) BI built around LookML, a real modeling language and governed semantic layer; stronger modeling/governance than Superset's lightweight layer, but commercial, locked-in, and priced for the enterprise.

first_choose_when: Choose a cluster wrapper when Redis Cluster slot routing is a hard requirement on top of this driver.
first_notes: Single-node lua-resty-redis is simpler; cluster routing adds another community layer.

first_choose_when: Choose lucidrains' implementations when you need another clean PyTorch reimplementation body with broader current coverage.
first_notes: Another prolific single-author body of clean PyTorch reimplementations spanning many architectures (incl. newer ones); often more actively updated, similar "read the code" value, broader/more current scope.

first_choose_when: Choose Luigi only when a lighter legacy Python pipeline library is enough and Airflow's scheduler/UI footprint is unnecessary.
first_notes: Spotify's older Python pipeline library; lighter and simpler, but largely superseded by Airflow with a much smaller community and weaker scheduling/UI.

first_choose_when: Choose built-in Spotlight when you want no install and can accept the limited stock query/answer surface.
first_notes: No install, supported, but the limited stock query/answer surface is exactly what Flashlight tried to extend.

first_choose_when: Pick Make when you want a proprietary cloud visual automation product and do not need self-hosting.
first_notes: Make is cloud-only and proprietary; n8n offers self-hosting and code extensibility.

first_choose_when: Choose manhole or remote pdb when you can embed the debug shell ahead of time instead of attaching after the fact.
first_notes: Cleaner and safer, but no help for an already-wedged process that lacks pre-instrumentation.

first_choose_when: Pick manual prompting when no tooling, full control, and zero infra matter more than measurement and reproducibility.
first_notes: No tooling, full control, zero infra; but unmeasured, non-reproducible, and exactly the toil SkillOpt automates.

first_choose_when: Pick a hosted product when you want the richer managed "work like Manus" experience and accept leaving the repo-local OSS path.
first_notes: The commercial pattern this skill imitates ("work like Manus"); managed and richer, but a hosted product, not an open, IDE-local, repo-committable skill.

first_choose_when: Choose MapServer for fast mature mapfile-configured OGC publishing; choose QGIS for desktop GIS workflows or when authors already maintain QGIS projects.
first_notes: Fast, mature C OGC map server; publishing-only, mapfile-configured; comparable to QGIS Server, not to the desktop.

first_choose_when: Choose Marigold when you need diffusion-based depth.
first_notes: Diffusion-based depth; can be high quality but slower with more parameters — V2 explicitly targets faster inference / fewer params.

first_choose_when: Choose a revival fork when you specifically need a community-maintained successor path, especially around Thunderbird.
first_notes: A community fork aimed at keeping the idea alive (notably for Thunderbird), as the original stalled; hosting and its own maintenance status should be verified before relying on it (see Caveats).

first_choose_when: Choose markdown-nice when you need a web editor for Markdown-to-WeChat/Zhihu styling.
first_notes: Web editor for Markdown→WeChat/Zhihu paste-ready styling; mature, no agent, theme-based not prompt-driven. HTML Anything reuses its `juice` inlining idea but adds agent generation + 9 surfaces.

first_choose_when: Choose markdown-to-image when you need Markdown-to-social-card PNG generation.
first_notes: Markdown→social-card-PNG generator; narrower output, also no local-agent model.

first_choose_when: Pick Marker when PDF-to-Markdown with DL layout models is enough and Docling's broader input spread is unnecessary.
first_notes: PDF→Markdown converter also using deep-learning layout models; similar gen-AI target, narrower input-format range than Docling's PDF/Office/HTML/image spread.

first_choose_when: Choose Marp when you need Markdown-to-slides with HTML/PDF/PPTX exports.
first_notes: Markdown→slides (HTML/PDF/PPTX) with a clean ecosystem and exports this skill lacks; far less visual flexibility per slide.

first_choose_when: The most popular React UI library with a Material Design aesthetic and a large enterprise presence.
first_notes: MUI is more ubiquitous in the West; Ant Design dominates in China and Asia-Pacific enterprise. Both are comprehensive; choose based on design language preference and regional ecosystem.

first_choose_when: Choose Mathpix when accuracy on handwriting, multiline equations, mobile capture, or document export outweighs SaaS cost and data residency; choose pix2tex when local MIT-licensed equation OCR is the constraint.
first_notes: Commercial math-OCR service/API; generally the accuracy leader for math + handwriting + multiline, with mobile apps and document export — but it's a paid SaaS (per-call cost, data leaves your machine), not an MIT self-hostable repo.

first_choose_when: Choose Maxwell's Daemon when you need a ready binlog-to-JSON daemon.
first_notes: Reads MySQL binlog and emits JSON to Kafka/Kinesis/etc.; a ready daemon rather than a library, narrower output model.

first_choose_when: Choose Mayan EDMS when workflow, versioning, and granular enterprise permissions are mandatory; choose paperless-ngx for a personal or small-team scan archive where OCR/search automation matters and ops must stay moderate.
first_notes: Also Python/Django, but a heavier enterprise EDMS with a real workflow engine, versioning and granular permissions; far steeper to operate and overkill for a personal scan archive. Apache-2.0 (more permissive than paperless's GPLv3).

first_choose_when: Choose mCaptcha when you want a self-hosted Rust PoW CAPTCHA with its own rate-limited difficulty model.
first_notes: Overlapping goal, different stack and ergonomics.

first_choose_when: Choose mdcat when you need a Rust CLI that renders Markdown to the terminal, including inline images on supporting terminals.
first_notes: Rust CLI that renders Markdown to the terminal, including inline images on supporting terminals; single binary, active.

first_choose_when: Choose mechanistic-interpretability tooling when you need feature-level understanding via patching/ablation.
first_notes: Studies circuits via activation patching/ablation on HF models for *understanding*; this repo is a coarse, capability-oriented "duplicate whole layer blocks in GGUF and measure" demo, not feature-level interp.

first_choose_when: Choose MediaPipe LLM Inference API when you want an easier same-org drop-in layer.
first_notes: Higher-level, easier drop-in on-device LLM from the same org using `.task` models, but less of a low-level orchestration layer and overlapping/superseded by LiteRT-LM in direction — the simpler-but-less-flexible sibling.

first_choose_when: Choose MediaPipe LLM Inference Studio when you need the older same-org demo/tooling path.
first_notes: The older same-org demo/tooling path for on-device LLMs; overlapping intent, superseded in direction by the LiteRT-based Gallery.

first_choose_when: Choose Megatron-LM for lower-level NVIDIA-style tensor and pipeline parallelism in very large transformer pretraining.
first_notes: Top-end throughput at scale, but more bespoke; Colossal-AI tries to make similar ideas more composable.

first_choose_when: Academic research project turned commercial for LLM memory management.
first_notes: Deep research roots in memory management for LLMs; commercial service with a different pricing and integration model.

first_choose_when: Pick Memgraph when you want an in-memory Cypher graph DB without the Redis-module operating model.
first_notes: In-memory, Cypher-compatible, streaming-focused graph DB; BSL-licensed. Overlaps FalkorDB's in-memory niche without the Redis-module model.

first_choose_when: Choose memray when an actively maintained profiler with flame graphs and live mode matters more than ncurses-style heap snapshots.
first_notes: Modern Python memory workflow, but you use its launch/attach tooling rather than memory-analyzer's GDB-driven report.

first_choose_when: Choose Mercury/Postlight Parser when you need a Node article parser that also fetches pages.
first_notes: Node article parser that also fetched pages; historically popular but maintenance has been uneven.

first_choose_when: Choose Metabase when simple deployment and non-SQL question building matter more than chart depth; choose Superset for warehouse BI teams that accept a multi-service stack.
first_notes: Open-source BI with a far simpler deploy (single jar/container) and a friendlier no-SQL question builder; easier for non-technical users, but a lighter semantic/customization story and less raw-SQL/chart depth than Superset.

first_choose_when: Choose T-MAC when you need the low-bit CPU kernel library beneath BitNet.
first_notes: The low-bit CPU kernel library whose lookup-table method BitNet builds on; a kernel/library layer, whereas BitNet is the packaged end-to-end ternary inference framework.

first_choose_when: Choose MiDaS/DPT when you need earlier widely used monocular-depth models.
first_notes: Earlier widely-used monocular-depth models; mature and permissively usable, but generally surpassed by Depth Anything V2 on detail/robustness. [推断]

first_choose_when: Closed-source cloud-only image generation services.
first_notes: Proprietary models, subscription-based, no local control; WebUI is open-source and runs on your own GPU.

first_choose_when: Choose Milvus when you need a distributed vector database with horizontal scale and metadata/control-plane features.
first_notes: Distributed vector database (often embedding FAISS/HNSW engines under the hood) with horizontal scale, metadata, and a control plane; heavier to run, but you don't build sharding/persistence.

first_choose_when: Choose Miniflux for a minimalist self-hosted Go backend and web reader; choose NetNewsWire when the value is a native macOS/iOS front end rather than operating a server.
first_notes: Minimalist self-hosted Go feed reader (server + web); single-binary backend, no native Apple app of its own.

first_choose_when: Choose MinIO for S3-compatible object storage consumed by programs and apps; keep copyparty for human-facing file sharing and ingest over browser, WebDAV, FTP, or SFTP.
first_notes: S3-compatible object storage for programmatic/app access. Different shape entirely — copyparty is a human-facing multi-protocol file server, not an object store.

first_choose_when: Choose mitmproxy when Python scripting plus CLI/TUI/web UI matter more than Node.js rules.
first_notes: Python, actively maintained, powerful scripting + TUI/web UI; the go-to programmable MITM proxy if you're not tied to Node.js.

project_or_alternative: MITRE ATT&CK Navigator / framework docs (read the source mappings yourself)
first_choose_when: Choose primary framework docs when authoritative current technique data matters more than agent workflows.
first_notes: Authoritative, always-current technique data, but no agent-executable workflow — you wire ATT&CK to procedure manually. This pack pre-binds workflows to (a snapshot of) those frameworks.

first_choose_when: Choose MLX when you need fast Apple-silicon inference with Python/Swift ergonomics.
first_notes: Fast Apple-silicon inference with clean Python/Swift ergonomics and broad model support, but Apple-only and not specialized for ternary 1-bit weights.

first_choose_when: Choose mlx-lm when you need Apple's own MLX LLM toolkit with a minimal server.
first_notes: Apple's own MLX LLM toolkit with a minimal OpenAI-compatible server — oMLX is built **on** mlx-lm's BatchGenerator; mlx-lm is lower-level and lacks the menu-bar app, tiered SSD cache, multi-model LRU, and admin dashboard.

first_choose_when: Choose Mockaroo when you need hosted, schema-first mock-data export rather than an in-process test library.
first_notes: Hosted SaaS / schema-first mock-data generator (CSV/JSON/SQL export) — not an in-process library; good for one-off bulk datasets, but it's a service, not a repo you embed in tests.

first_choose_when: Choose modern agent frameworks when you need current standardized tool access for LLMs.
first_notes: Current, standardized way to give an LLM tools; far better orchestration, structured tool I/O, and active support than this bespoke demo.

project_or_alternative: Modern multimodal LLMs (GPT-4o / Gemini / Claude vision / Qwen-VL)
first_choose_when: Choose modern multimodal LLMs when you need native vision inside one maintained model.
first_notes: Native vision in a single model — captioning, VQA, generation/editing via the model or its built-in tools; no foundation-model zoo to host, actively maintained. This is what replaced the whole TaskMatrix pattern.

first_choose_when: Choose Moirai when you need another open time-series foundation model with multivariate framing.
first_notes: Another open time-series foundation model with multivariate framing; overlapping use case, different architecture and license terms.

first_choose_when: Choose Morphic or Perplexity when you need hosted/proprietary answer engines.
first_notes: Hosted/proprietary answer engines; no self-hosting or provider choice, opposite of Vane's privacy/self-host pitch.

first_choose_when: Choose Motion or Framer Motion for React-first declarative component animation; choose Anime.js when imperative, framework-agnostic orchestration is the better fit.
first_notes: Declarative, React-first (also a vanilla `motion` core); idiomatic for component-driven apps. Anime.js is imperative and framework-agnostic — better when you're not living inside React's render model.

first_choose_when: Choose Motion One when the smallest WAAPI-based runtime is the priority; choose Anime.js when timelines, draggable, SVG, scroll, and text helpers justify more surface area.
first_notes: Tiny WAAPI-based animator; very small footprint. Anime.js offers more built-ins (timeline, draggable, SVG morph, scroll, text) at a larger but still light cost.

first_choose_when: Choose Mozilla fathom or custom ML when you need roll-your-own learned extraction.
first_notes: Roll-your-own learned extraction; more control, far more work than adopting dragnet's models.

first_choose_when: Choose Mozilla Readability when you are building your own parser or reader mode; choose Just Read when you need a ready-to-use browser extension despite its EULA/source-available status.
first_notes: The open-source MPL parsing engine behind many reader modes; a library to build on, not a ready-to-use extension.

first_choose_when: Choose a multi-stage or hand-optimized Dockerfile when you own the source-level build and want predictability.
first_notes: The source-level fix: smallest, most predictable, fully under your control — but requires owning and editing every build. SlimToolkit's pitch is "no Dockerfile change."

first_choose_when: Choose mypyc when standard type-annotated Python is the source of truth and Cython-specific syntax is unacceptable.
first_notes: Closer to "compile my Python" with standard typing, but younger and narrower than Cython.

first_choose_when: Choose generic image-prompt packs when raw model access is enough.
first_notes: Generic image-prompt collections give you raw model access with no article-analysis, shot-list, or consistent-IP layer this skill adds.

first_choose_when: Choose nanochat when you need the full single-GPU GPT training project this is simplified from.
first_notes: The full single-GPU GPT training project this is simplified from; meant for humans to train a real small ChatGPT clone end-to-end, not for an agent to mutate under a time budget.

first_choose_when: Choose nanoGPT when you need a minimal GPT training reference.
first_notes: Minimal GPT training reference; pedagogical baseline you edit by hand, with no agentic-research framing or fixed-budget evaluation harness.

first_choose_when: Choose the original Flashlight repo only when you specifically need the upstream this fork descends from.
first_notes: The upstream this descends from; also unmaintained — the fork chain (w0lfschild and others) exists precisely because the original stalled.

first_choose_when: Choose native embed when you only need to display an existing PDF with zero integration work.
first_notes: Zero-dependency display, but no generation, no programmatic control, and inconsistent across browsers.

first_choose_when: Browser-native approach with zero dependencies but no reactivity or DX.
first_notes: Native DOM is verbose and error-prone; Lit gives you reactive templates and a component base class with minimal overhead.

first_choose_when: Choose native OpenSSH or autossh for durable tunnels that need config fidelity, speed, and optional auto-reconnect.
first_notes: More robust for production, but managed as a process rather than an in-Python object.

project_or_alternative: Native agent memory (`CLAUDE.md`, Cursor rules, Codex `AGENTS.md`)
first_choose_when: Pick native memory files when static always-loaded instructions are enough.
first_notes: Built-in, always loaded, no extra install — but a static instruction file, not a per-task evolving plan with progress logging and a stop gate.

first_choose_when: Choose native Query DSL when you need maximum version-native power and control.
first_notes: Maximum power and control, version-native, but verbose JSON with a steep learning curve — the friction this project removes.

first_choose_when: Choose direct system clients when you have committed to one broker or stream.
first_notes: Simpler for a single system, but no broker-agnostic layer.

first_choose_when: Choose NeMo when you need a larger, GPU/scale-oriented conversational-AI toolkit with NVIDIA tooling.
first_notes: Strong ASR/TTS and NVIDIA integration, but heavier and more vendor-centric than SpeechBrain's lighter research framing.

first_choose_when: Pick Neo4j when the largest property-graph ecosystem matters more than Redis embedding or sparse-matrix speed.
first_notes: Industry-standard property graph with the largest ecosystem (Bolt, GDS, APOC); heavier, GPLv3/commercial. FalkorDB is faster on sparse-matrix traversals and Redis-embedded but younger and SSPL.

first_choose_when: Choose Neo4j directly when you need the graph database layer and will build ingestion yourself.
first_notes: The graph database this project stores into; production-grade storage + Cypher, but you build the entire NLP ingestion pipeline yourself — AgriKG is precisely that pipeline as an example.

first_choose_when: Modal terminal editor with modern Lua configuration.
first_notes: Neovim is terminal-only and has a steep learning curve; VS Code is GUI-first and beginner-friendly.

first_choose_when: Pick Neptune when you want a managed AWS graph service and accept cloud lock-in over self-hosting.
first_notes: Managed, multi-model (Gremlin/openCypher/SPARQL) graph service; no self-host, AWS lock-in. FalkorDB is self-hostable OSS-adjacent.

first_choose_when: Choose hosted VMAF scorers when you need managed quality scoring.
first_notes: Hosted quality-scoring services; convenience over running metrics yourself, with vendor dependence.

first_choose_when: Lightweight alternative to Electron with smaller footprint.
first_notes: Smaller than Electron but less mature ecosystem and fewer platform features than Tauri.

first_choose_when: Choose NewsBlur when you want a hosted/open-source service stack with training or intelligence features; choose NetNewsWire when local-first native reading is the core requirement.
first_notes: Open-source hosted reader with training/intelligence features; a full service stack vs NetNewsWire's local-first native client.

first_choose_when: Choose newspaper3k or goose3 when you need article extraction with built-in fetching and metadata.
first_notes: Article-extraction libraries with built-in fetching and metadata; convenient but historically uneven maintenance.

first_choose_when: Choose newspaper4k when you need the actively maintained fork of this project.
first_notes: The actively-maintained fork of this very project; same API lineage, bug fixes and Python-version updates — the recommended successor.

first_choose_when: Choose Nextcloud when you need the full self-hosted cloud shape: sync clients, apps, sharing, and groupware; keep copyparty when portability, protocol breadth, and no database matter more than an app ecosystem.
first_notes: Full self-hosted "cloud" (files, sync clients, apps, sharing, optional OCR via add-ons) but a heavy PHP/DB/Redis stack. copyparty is dramatically lighter and faster to stand up, with no two-way sync and no app ecosystem.

first_choose_when: File-sync-first with a photo viewer; not a dedicated photo management app.
first_notes: Nextcloud is a general file server with photo plugins; Immich is purpose-built for media with AI search and mobile auto-backup.

first_choose_when: Choose built-in NGINX buffering when first-party config matters more than offloading multipart parsing from the app.
first_notes: Simpler to keep working, but the app still parses uploads and gets less offload than this module provides.

first_choose_when: Choose a C module when maximum control and performance justify writing C and recompiling NGINX for every change.
first_notes: This is the high-friction path ngx_lua exists to avoid.

first_choose_when: Choose njs when first-party NGINX JavaScript scripting is more important than the Lua/OpenResty ecosystem.
first_notes: Simpler to install and official, but smaller and less mature than the Lua/OpenResty world.

first_choose_when: The incumbent JS/TS runtime with the largest ecosystem.
first_notes: Node.js has the deepest ecosystem and broadest hosting support; Bun is faster but younger and less proven.

first_choose_when: Choose notebooklm-mcp when persistent MCP sessions across tools matter more than a single Claude Code skill.
first_notes: The MCP-server sibling: persistent chat sessions, TypeScript/npm, and multi-tool support (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor). Choose it for stateful research across tools; choose this skill for a zero-server, Python, Claude-Code-only clone-and-go install.

project_or_alternative: npm / pnpm packaging a skill dir
first_choose_when: Choose npm/pnpm packaging when you want JS-ecosystem versioning and lockfiles.
first_notes: Reuses the JS package ecosystem (real versioning + lockfiles), but skills aren't npm-shaped and you'd hand-place files per agent; Skills is purpose-built for the `SKILL.md` layout.

first_choose_when: Choose Numba for decorator-based numeric JIT when array/loop kernels matter more than extension ABI or C/C++ wrapping.
first_notes: No separate C build and strong for numeric kernels, but narrower in scope and tied to a runtime-JIT model.

first_choose_when: Full-stack Vue framework — the Vue ecosystem's equivalent of Next.js.
first_notes: Nuxt is for Vue teams; Next.js is for React teams. The choice is usually determined by your UI framework preference.

first_choose_when: Choose objgraph when reference graphs from inside the process are the main diagnostic need.
first_notes: Useful for chasing what keeps objects alive, but in-process rather than an external GDB attach.

first_choose_when: Choose editor Markdown plugins for first-class Markdown authoring with live preview inside a document editor.
first_notes: First-class Markdown authoring with live preview, but inside a *document editor*, not your webmail compose box; you'd draft there and paste, losing the in-field, at-send-time conversion.

first_choose_when: Use Vaultwarden for lightweight, unofficial self-hosted password management with Bitwarden client compatibility; choose the official Bitwarden for upstream support, SSO, compliance, and a larger team.
first_notes: Official support, SSO, compliance, and a larger team — but the self-hosted version is heavier (MSSQL, .NET) and the free tier is cloud-only.

first_choose_when: Choose official paper repos when you need the authors' own implementations.
first_notes: The authors' own implementations — paper-accurate weights and numbers, but each is its own codebase with its own style/quirks; not a single consistently-written collection for browsing many GANs side by side.

first_choose_when: Choose official WeChat when account safety and clean updates beat tweak features.
first_notes: The supported path: no anti-revoke, no auto-reply, no multi-instance, but it updates cleanly, isn't a ban risk, and doesn't inject foreign code into your messenger. The honest default for anyone who values the account.

first_choose_when: Choose Ollama when you need the default cross-platform local LLM runner and broad model library.
first_notes: The default Mac/cross-platform local-LLM runner (llama.cpp-based), huge ecosystem and model library; broader OS support but no Apple-MLX backend and a simpler caching story than oMLX's tiered hot/cold KV cache.

first_choose_when: Use SGLang for datacenter throughput serving with structured generation; choose Ollama/llama.cpp for lightweight local/edge inference on CPU or consumer GPUs.
first_notes: Portable C/C++ inference engine (GGUF) running everywhere including Macs and phones; not a datacenter multi-GPU throughput engine.

first_choose_when: Choose ONNX Runtime when you need vendor-neutral format/backend breadth.
first_notes: Vendor-neutral, mature, many formats and backends across ecosystems, but heavier, less tuned for the latest small mobile LLMs, and lacks LiteRT-LM's Gemma-specific mobile quantization wins.

first_choose_when: Choose OPA or OpenFGA for cross-service, language-agnostic authorization at scale; choose django-rules when policy is local to a Django app and should stay in process.
first_notes: External, language-agnostic policy/authorization services (Rego / Zanzibar-style relationships); powerful at scale and across services, far heavier than an in-process Django lib.

first_choose_when: Choose Open Deep Research when you need an API-model reproduction of a deep-research agent.
first_notes: Open reproduction of a deep-research agent over an API model; similar open spirit, different stack and (usually) no self-hosted fine-tuned weights.

first_choose_when: Choose Open Deep Research when framework-backed reference agents and ecosystem matter more.
first_notes: Framework-backed reference agents with bigger ecosystems and tooling; heavier to read and adapt than this single-file-ish implementation.

first_choose_when: Choose hosted embedding APIs when no self-hosting/GPU and strong managed quality matter most.
first_notes: Hosted, no self-hosting or GPU, strong quality — but paid, network-dependent, and sends text to a third party; text2vec runs fully local.

first_choose_when: Choose hosted Deep Research products when turnkey quality and no GPU matter most.
first_notes: Hosted, turnkey, strong quality, no GPU to run; but closed, paid per use, no self-hosting or model control — the opposite tradeoff to MiroThinker.

first_choose_when: Choose OpenAI Codex CLI when you want the canonical upstream that Open Interpreter forks.
first_notes: The **upstream** Open Interpreter forks. Canonical, larger team, faster mainline; tuned for OpenAI models. Open Interpreter adds the swappable low-cost-model harness layer on top and tracks Codex's `main`.

first_choose_when: Choose hosted computer-use products when turnkey proprietary vision agents are acceptable.
first_notes: Hosted vision computer-use agents — turnkey but proprietary, tied to one model vendor; Cua is the open self-hostable infra layer (and can *run* such models via liteLLM).

first_choose_when: Choose OpenAI Whisper when you need to generate subtitles from audio, not retime an existing subtitle file.
first_notes: Generates subtitles from audio (transcription), a different job — useful when you have *no* subtitle file; overkill and lossy when you already have correct text that's merely mistimed.

first_choose_when: Choose OpenCLIP when you need open training code plus a large checkpoint zoo.
first_notes: Open reproduction with training code and a large zoo of checkpoints (many trained on LAION/DataComp); the de-facto choice when you need more or stronger CLIP models or want to train your own — strictly broader than this reference repo.

first_choose_when: Choose OpenCV when computer vision or frame-level image processing is the primary task, with video as a side effect.
first_notes: Computer vision first; can read/write video but lacks editing concepts like clips, transitions, or compositing layers.

first_choose_when: Choose OpenDocMan only for basic PHP/MySQL business file control on an existing PHP stack; keep paperless-ngx when the core job is searchable OCR archival.
first_notes: PHP/MySQL DMS for business file control + access rules; dated UI, no first-class OCR/auto-tagging — only if you need simple web access control on an existing PHP stack.

first_choose_when: Choose OpenKG or CN-DBpedia when you need Chinese open knowledge-graph data/resources.
first_notes: Chinese open knowledge-graph data/resources; data sources rather than a runnable pipeline+UI.

first_choose_when: Choose OpenResty when you want the supported consumption path: matched NGINX, LuaJIT, this module, and lua-resty libraries together.
first_notes: In practice this is how many teams consume ngx_lua; this repo is one component inside that distribution.

first_choose_when: Choose OpenSearch SQL when you run OpenSearch and need its own SQL/PPL plugin.
first_notes: The OpenSearch fork's own SQL/PPL plugin; the analogous answer if you run OpenSearch instead of Elastic.

first_choose_when: Choose OpenTelemetry Collector when you need vendor-neutral routing for metrics, traces, and logs.
first_notes: Vendor-neutral, CNCF-governed router for metrics **and** traces/logs with broad receiver/exporter set; heavier config model, stronger tracing story, overlapping metrics scope.

first_choose_when: Use OpenTimelineIO for timeline interchange between apps (Adobe's format); use MLT for actual rendering and playback engine.
first_notes: Adobe's timeline interchange format — solves "export timeline from app A to app B", not rendering or playback itself. [未验证]

first_choose_when: Choose Optuna or Ax when you need Bayesian/surrogate optimization for expensive evaluations or HPO.
first_notes: Bayesian/surrogate optimization, ideal for expensive evaluations and HPO; different paradigm (sample-efficient, not population-based) — complementary, not a drop-in.

first_choose_when: Choose logrotate or cron for non-Airflow log files, not for metadata pruning or zombie-task cleanup.
first_notes: Handles log files outside Airflow, but can't safely prune the metadata DB or kill zombie tasks the way an Airflow-aware DAG can.

first_choose_when: Choose OSWorld or WebArena when you need evaluation environments rather than a runnable sandbox.
first_notes: Evaluation environments Cua-Bench targets — they grade agents; Cua provides the runnable sandbox + agent that gets graded.

first_choose_when: Choose live forks when working code survival matters more than this gutted repo.
first_notes: Where working code survives; PyCoreDev (2023-02) retains full code + `package.json`. None are large or clearly maintained — pick by recency and read the diff yourself.

first_choose_when: Choose oxlint when the need is a fast Rust linter host; choose React Doctor when you need the React-specific rule pack that can run through oxlint.
first_notes: The fast Rust linter React Doctor ships a plugin for; oxlint is the engine/host, React Doctor supplies the React-specific agent-facing rule pack.

first_choose_when: Choose PaddleNLP/ERNIE when you need Baidu's actively maintained successor NLP stack on Paddle 2.x.
first_notes: Baidu's actively-maintained successor NLP stack on Paddle 2.x; where current Baidu NLP (incl. sentiment) development actually happens — Senta is the older, frozen sibling.

first_choose_when: Choose PaddleOCR for complex layouts, photos, CJK-heavy workloads, or table/layout structure; choose Tesseract for clean printed text where offline CPU deployment and mature bindings matter more.
first_notes: Deep-learning OCR + layout/table/structure models; far stronger on complex layouts, photos, and CJK, but heavier deps (PaddlePaddle), Apache-2.0, GPU-helpful — a fuller pipeline vs Tesseract's single recognizer.

first_choose_when: Choose paid providers when production SLAs, residential IPs, and rotation matter.
first_notes: Commercial residential/datacenter pools with SLAs and rotation — the production answer; haipproxy only fits when you specifically need a self-hosted *distributed* free pool.

first_choose_when: Choose paid proxy services when production needs SLAs, clean IP ranges, and support.
first_notes: Commercial residential/datacenter/ISP proxies with SLAs, large clean IP ranges, and support — reliable and fast, but paid (often metered per-GB) and not open-source. The right call for production.

first_choose_when: Pick pandas-datareader when the source set is mostly Western/global and DataFrame ergonomics are enough.
first_notes: Maintained generic reader for (mostly Western) economic/market sources into DataFrames; same DataFrame ergonomics, different (global) source set.

first_choose_when: Choose Pandoc when you need universal document conversion, not just Markdown parsing or conformance tests.
first_notes: The universal document converter; can read/write dozens of formats, but it's a heavy CLI tool, not a JS library.

first_choose_when: Choose pandoc + pager when you need heavyweight general-purpose conversion across many formats.
first_notes: Converts Markdown to many formats (heavyweight, general-purpose); overkill for "just show this .md in my terminal".

first_choose_when: Choose Parquet plus zstd/snappy when you need the mainstream columnar-at-rest path.
first_notes: The mainstream columnar-at-rest path: schema-aware encodings (dictionary/RLE) plus a block codec. Mature and ubiquitous; OpenZL is a lower-level framework letting you build custom codec graphs, not a file format with an ecosystem.

first_choose_when: Use Vaultwarden for full-featured personal and team password management with Bitwarden client compatibility; choose Passbolt when you need an open-source team password manager focused on collaboration and access control.
first_notes: Purpose-built for team sharing with built-in access controls; less mature client ecosystem than Bitwarden.

first_choose_when: Python package manager with PEP 582 support.
first_notes: pdm is modern and spec-compliant; uv is faster but may lack some pdm-specific workflow features.

first_choose_when: Choose built-in agent history when native zero-install recall is enough.
first_notes: Native and zero-install, but single-agent and no cross-tool search/cost rollup — the gap AgentsView fills.

first_choose_when: Choose Perplexica when you need Vane's direct predecessor by the same author.
first_notes: Vane's direct predecessor by the same author; same SearxNG+RAG core. Choosing Vane = choosing the maintained continuation.

first_choose_when: Choose hosted research SaaS when quality and zero ops outweigh privacy/local control.
first_notes: Hosted SaaS, strong quality and zero ops — but your queries and context leave your machine, the opposite of LDR's premise.

first_choose_when: Choose pgvector when you need vector search inside Postgres with SQL, transactions, and metadata filtering.
first_notes: Vector search *inside Postgres* (IVFFlat/HNSW) with SQL, transactions, and metadata filtering for free; simpler if your data already lives in Postgres, slower/less flexible than a tuned FAISS index at large scale.

first_choose_when: Pick a vector store when classic embedding + ANN retrieval is sufficient and cheaper at scale.
first_notes: Classic embedding + ANN vector retrieval; cheaper at scale and breadth, but exactly the "similarity ≠ relevance" failure mode PageIndex is built to avoid.

first_choose_when: Choose Phi-3.5-vision when Microsoft tooling/backing matters for a small vision model.
first_notes: Small, capable vision model with strong MS tooling/backing; competitive on image tasks, weaker/narrower video-and-speech story than the MiniCPM-o line.

first_choose_when: Self-hosted photo management with strong RAW support and a focus on privacy.
first_notes: PhotoPrism has a more mature RAW pipeline and broader format support; Immich has a more modern mobile app and faster feature velocity.

first_choose_when: Choose raw Pillow when the CAPTCHA should be tiny custom drawing code you own end-to-end.
first_notes: This library prepackages the same text/noise rendering idea with audio support and sensible defaults.

first_choose_when: Choose Pillow + a small custom script when you want the DIY route asciify itself embodies.
first_notes: The DIY route asciify itself embodies; with no license on asciify, rolling your own from Pillow is often the cleaner, legally-clear option.

first_choose_when: Python's default package installer.
first_notes: pip is universal and stable but slow; uv is 10–100x faster with a modern resolver and lockfile.

first_choose_when: Choose plain markdown when zero dependencies and readability matter more than dependency metadata.
first_notes: Zero-dependency and human-readable, but no dependency metadata, no GitHub sync, no parallel-stream isolation — the unstructured baseline CCPM replaces.

first_choose_when: Pick manual files when zero install and total ownership matter more than lifecycle hooks or completion gates.
first_notes: Zero install and fully yours, but no lifecycle hooks, no auto re-injection after `/clear`, no completion gate, no session catchup — exactly the manual workflow this skill automates.

first_choose_when: Choose raw ADB when you only need the screencap/input mechanism Douyin-Bot demonstrates.
first_notes: The underlying mechanism Douyin-Bot demonstrates; if you only want screencap + input events, raw `adb` is more transparent and isn't tied to a dead cloud API.

first_choose_when: Choose Docker or containerd when ubiquitous containers are enough.
first_notes: Ubiquitous and trusted, but gives you a container, not a sandbox protocol, credential vault, egress policy, or multi-language SDK surface.

project_or_alternative: Plain Git + agent's own session logs
first_choose_when: Choose plain Git and native logs when zero extra tooling matters more than unified provenance.
first_notes: Zero extra tooling, but agent logs are scattered per-tool, not linked to commits, not uniformly rewindable, and clutter or never reach the repo. Entire is the unifying capture/index layer.

first_choose_when: Choose plain logging or print when you need zero dependency and machine-parseable output.
first_notes: Zero dependency and trivially machine-parseable; no ETA/rate/in-place redraw, and noisy for interactive use — the right call for files/CI, the wrong one for a human watching a TTY.

first_choose_when: Choose plain markdown when zero dependencies and human-readable notes matter more than structure.
first_notes: Zero deps and human-readable, but no dependency graph, no ready-detection, no merge-safe IDs — exactly the unstructured approach beads replaces.

first_choose_when: Choose plain pgvector when full schema and retrieval control outweigh Mem0's packaged layer.
first_notes: Full control, no extra dependency or platform; you build and maintain the extraction prompts, schema, and retrieval that Mem0 gives you out of the box.

first_choose_when: Choose plain PyTorch when portability and hiring pool matter more than a vertically integrated engine.
first_notes: The default, maximally-portable, maximally-hireable stack for both serving and custom kernels; you assemble performance yourself rather than buying a vertically-integrated engine.

first_choose_when: Choose plain tmux plus git worktree scripts when zero dependencies and full scriptability matter most.
first_notes: Zero-dependency and fully scriptable, but you hand-roll the worktree lifecycle, agent adapters, live state UI, and CI/review/conflict routing — exactly the glue Agent Orchestrator packages.

first_choose_when: Choose a plain vector DB when owning schema and retrieval outweighs augmentation features.
first_notes: You own the schema and retrieval; no augmentation, no entity model, no cloud — maximum control, maximum wiring.

first_choose_when: Pick PlantUML when the DSL must cover many UML and flowchart types and server/Java rendering is acceptable.
first_notes: Text DSL covering many UML + flowchart types, usually server/Java-rendered; richer diagram catalog but not a browser-native JS library.

first_choose_when: Choose managed-service retention knobs when supported safety matters more than custom cleanup coverage.
first_notes: Managed services expose their own log/metadata retention knobs; less flexible but supported and safer than custom DELETEs.

first_choose_when: Choose Platypus when you need another Python multi-objective EA library.
first_notes: Another Python multi-objective EA library; smaller scope/community than pymoo's algorithm + tooling breadth. [推断]

first_choose_when: Choose Playwright when you need modern cross-engine automation with auto-wait, tracing, and multi-language bindings.
first_notes: Modern cross-engine automation (Chromium/Firefox/WebKit) with auto-wait, network interception, tracing, multi-language bindings; everything PhantomJS did and far more, actively maintained — the recommended modern choice.

first_choose_when: Choose Playwright when you need cross-browser deterministic automation for portable CI.
first_notes: Cross-browser (Chromium/Firefox/WebKit), deterministic, code-or-MCP driven, headless-capable; the go-to for portable automation/CI. Chrome DevTools MCP trades breadth for Chrome-native DevTools depth (traces, Lighthouse, heap, CrUX).

first_choose_when: Choose Playwright when you need maintained real-browser automation for JS-heavy pages.
first_notes: Real, maintained headless-browser automation (Chromium/Firefox/WebKit) for JS-heavy pages; far more robust than `requests-html`'s pyppeteer `render()`, but heavier and a different (browser-driving) mental model. Pair with selectolax/bs4 for parsing.

first_choose_when: Choose Playwright or Puppeteer when you want mature code-first Node automation libraries.
first_notes: Mature Node.js automation libraries with cross-browser support and rich APIs — but you import them as code and write/maintain selectors; Agent Browser is a CLI with LLM-friendly refs and no per-command launch cost.

first_choose_when: Dedicated package managers with mature workspaces.
first_notes: pnpm and Yarn have deep workspace and monorepo features; Bun's package manager is fast but may lack some advanced features.

first_choose_when: Choose Pocket, Instapaper, or Wallabag when the job is a durable read-it-later library; choose Just Read for immediate in-place article cleanup without building an archive workflow.
first_notes: Read-it-later services with durable cross-device libraries; heavier (account + backend) and aimed at saving, not in-place reformatting (Wallabag is self-hostable).

first_choose_when: Python dependency management and packaging.
first_notes: Poetry has mature project management and publish workflows; uv is faster but newer and still building feature parity.

first_choose_when: Choose polling when you lack binlog privileges and can accept missed deletes, load, and lag.
first_notes: No binlog privileges needed and trivially simple, but misses deletes, adds query load, and lags — the limitation CDC removes.

first_choose_when: Choose Portainer when the job is specifically Docker/Kubernetes container management through a web UI.
first_notes: Web UI focused specifically on Docker/Kubernetes container management; Cockpit's container view (Podman) is one tab among many, not the whole product.

first_choose_when: Choose Postlight Reader when cleaner open-source licensing matters more than active feature work; choose Just Read when selector memory and edit/highlight features are worth the licensing tradeoff.
first_notes: Open-source readability extension/parser; cleaner licensing story, but less actively maintained and fewer edit/highlight features.

first_choose_when: Choose PowerJob when a newer Java distributed scheduler/compute platform with richer workflow/DAG and map-reduce-style execution is worth a smaller install base.
first_notes: Often pitched as a more modern XXL-JOB alternative, but adoption is smaller. [未验证]

first_choose_when: Choose PR-Agent when you need an OSS assistant that posts summaries, Q&A, and comments directly to GitHub/GitLab MRs.
first_notes: OSS PR assistant that posts to GitHub/GitLab MRs directly and does summaries/Q&A; Open Code Review prints structured findings and leans on a deterministic positioning layer rather than MR integration.

first_choose_when: Choose Prefect when dynamic Python flows and lighter local development matter more than Airflow's provider breadth and familiar DAG scheduler.
first_notes: Pythonic, dynamic flows with lighter local-dev ergonomics and a hybrid/managed control plane; smaller operator ecosystem and a different (flow/task) model than Airflow's DAG files.

first_choose_when: Use Premiere Pro for Adobe-ecosystem professional editing; not comparable as an open-source embeddable framework.
first_notes: Commercial Adobe NLE; subscription-only, closed-source, and part of a Creative Cloud workflow.

first_choose_when: Choose Presto or Trino when you need a full ANSI-SQL engine federating ES with other sources.
first_notes: Full ANSI-SQL engine that can federate ES with other sources; far heavier to operate, but real SQL semantics and JOINs across stores.

first_choose_when: Choose progressbar2 when you need an older, configurable widget-style progress-bar library.
first_notes: Older, configurable progress-bar library; widget-based API is more verbose than `tqdm(iterable)`, smaller modern adoption.

first_choose_when: Choose Prometheus + node_exporter when you need pull-based scraping with its own TSDB and query language.
first_notes: Pull-based scraping with its own TSDB and query language; great for cloud-native metrics, but exporters are per-concern and it isn't a general push collector for logs/industrial protocols.

first_choose_when: Choose prompt_toolkit when you need powerful interactive prompts, REPLs, or input-heavy full-screen apps.
first_notes: Powerful for interactive prompts/REPLs and some full-screen apps; strong line-editing, but a different focus (input) and no ASCII-effects engine.

first_choose_when: Pick these methods when you want LLM-driven prompt search/evolution rather than validation-gated reusable skills.
first_notes: LLM-driven prompt-search/evolution methods; overlap on automated prompt improvement, but typically prompt strings, not validation-gated reusable skill artifacts.

first_choose_when: Choose PromptLayer for hosted prompt registry and request logging; keep Pezzo only when you specifically need self-hosted prompt management and accept a likely stalled codebase.
first_notes: Prompt registry + request logging; overlapping prompt-management scope, hosted-first.

first_choose_when: Choose Prophet when you need simple decomposition-based forecasting for business seasonality.
first_notes: Decomposition-based forecasting, trivial to use for business seasonality; not a deep-learning/LSTM demonstration.

first_choose_when: Commercial per-app proxy routing.
first_notes: Proxifier is a paid tool for routing specific apps; Clash Verge Rev is a system-level proxy client with rule-based routing.

first_choose_when: Choose Proxyman when modern macOS/cross-platform GUI polish matters most.
first_notes: Modern macOS/cross-platform GUI proxy; great UX, freemium, not a Node.js library you embed.

first_choose_when: Pick Pushshift-style clients for historical bulk Reddit archives when that data source is available.
first_notes: Historical bulk Reddit data (when Pushshift access is available); complements rather than replaces the live-API wrapper.

first_choose_when: Choose PSNR or SSIM when you need simple, fast signal-fidelity metrics.
