first_notes: Classic metrics; cheap and ubiquitous but correlate poorly with perceived quality. SSIMULACRA2 is specifically designed for better human correlation.

first_choose_when: Choose Puppeteer when you need the lower-level Chrome/CDP library this server builds on.
first_notes: The lower-level Chrome/CDP automation library this server is built on; you write the script, no MCP/agent layer or curated performance-insight tools.

first_choose_when: Choose Pushshift dumps or PRAW scripts when you want to bypass tooling and build directly on data/API access.
first_notes: Going straight to data dumps or the API yourself bypasses tooling and the ~1000 cap (dumps) but is roll-your-own — BDFR packages resolvers, dedup, naming, and logging for you.

first_choose_when: Choose py-amqp or pika when you need lower-level AMQP-only clients.
first_notes: Less abstraction and no multi-broker portability, but fewer moving parts if you will only ever use RabbitMQ.

first_choose_when: Choose py-spy when observe-only sampling is enough and avoiding code injection is the priority.
first_notes: Great for "where's the time/why is it stuck," but it cannot run arbitrary code in the target.

first_choose_when: Use Whisper when you need transcription text; use pyannote.audio when you need speaker diarization. They are complementary, not substitutes.
first_notes: Speaker diarization toolkit (who spoke when), not transcription. Often used together with Whisper.

first_choose_when: Choose pybind11 or nanobind when the performance-critical code is already C++ and Python only needs bindings.
first_notes: Ideal for C++ libraries, but you write C++, not a Python superset.

first_choose_when: Choose Pydantic AI when you need a type-safe, Pydantic-centric framework for structured outputs.
first_notes: Type-safe, Pydantic-centric agent framework emphasizing structured/validated outputs; smolagents leans into code-as-action instead of schema-validated tool calls.

first_choose_when: Choose pyfiglet when you need a pure-Python FIGlet port with the canonical figlet font set.
first_notes: Pure-Python port of FIGlet with the canonical figlet font set; the standard if you specifically want FIGlet fonts/compatibility, narrower scope (no decor/art-piece catalog).

first_choose_when: Choose pygame-ce when faster releases, newer SDL support, or tutorial compatibility point at the fork; choose pygame when the original package name and long-standing ecosystem are safer for your course or dependency chain.
first_notes: A community fork of this same library with a faster release cadence and newer SDL support; API-compatible enough that the choice is mostly about maintenance velocity and which one your tutorials target. [未验证]

first_choose_when: Choose pyglet when OpenGL-first windowing, multimedia, or light 3D support matters; choose pygame when SDL-backed 2D teaching material and beginner ecosystem matter more.
first_notes: Pure-Python, OpenGL-based windowing/multimedia library; no SDL dependency, supports 3D via OpenGL, but a smaller teaching community than pygame.

first_choose_when: Choose Pympler when an embedded library for per-type object sizes/counts is enough.
first_notes: It is one of memory-analyzer's dependencies, but it runs inside code you control rather than acting as an external attach tool.

first_choose_when: Low-level Python PDF library for extraction and manipulation.
first_notes: A library for direct PDF page manipulation, not a high-level Markdown converter; more powerful but requires more code.

first_choose_when: Pick low-level PDF libraries when speed and light footprint matter more than built-in layout/table fidelity.
first_notes: Fast, lightweight low-level PDF text/geometry extraction with no heavy models; you build layout/table logic yourself — less fidelity out of the box, far lighter footprint.

first_choose_when: Choose pynput when you need lower-level cross-platform input control or global hotkey monitoring.
first_notes: No screenshot/image-locate layer; it is smaller in scope than PyAutoGUI and focuses on input events.

first_choose_when: Choose PyPy for whole-program no-code-change JIT experiments before hand-Cythonizing targeted modules.
first_notes: Can speed whole programs, but C-extension compatibility and ecosystem fit can be the catch.

first_choose_when: Choose raw gdb plus CPython helpers when you want manual attach/inspect control and can wire the injection yourself.
first_notes: Pyrasite packages the inject-and-run-snippet workflow; raw gdb is lower-level and more manual.

first_choose_when: Choose the Python kernel when you do not specifically need Go and want the lowest-friction Jupyter/data-science ecosystem.
first_notes: Full ecosystem and default support, but it does not teach or execute Go.

first_choose_when: Choose Python Faker when your tests or seeders are Python rather than JavaScript.
first_notes: The same idea for Python (the JS Faker lineage descends from it); use it when your tests/seeders are Python, not JS.

first_choose_when: Choose python-social-auth when backend breadth and multi-framework social auth are the priority; choose Authomatic when you want a smaller in-process client and can tolerate lower activity.
first_notes: Multi-framework social-auth with many backends; broader provider list, heavier and framework-coupling per integration.

first_choose_when: Choose PyTorch FSDP when native fully-sharded data parallelism is enough and avoiding another framework matters.
first_notes: Built into PyTorch; Colossal-AI adds tensor/pipeline/sequence parallelism and Gemini offload at the cost of a dependency.

first_choose_when: Choose pywinauto when you are Windows-only and need the UI Automation / Win32 accessibility tree.
first_notes: Element-aware and far more robust than pixels, but not cross-platform and a steeper API.

first_choose_when: Choose Qdrant when you need a Rust vector database with payload filtering and persistence.
first_notes: Rust vector *database* with payload filtering, persistence, gRPC/REST API, sharding/replication; turnkey ops where FAISS is a bare library you wrap and operate yourself.

first_choose_when: Choose Quartz when you need an embeddable Java scheduler library inside your app, not a management platform.
first_notes: Powerful cron/trigger model but **no out-of-the-box admin UI, no distributed dispatcher, no run console**. XXL-JOB is closer to "Quartz + a management platform" in spirit.

first_choose_when: Choose Qwen-VL when you need a strong open vision-language family across sizes.
first_notes: Strong open vision-language family across sizes; broader size range and ecosystem, but the smallest tiers aren't as single-mindedly tuned for phone-class on-device footprint as MiniCPM-V.

first_choose_when: Choose upstream when original lineage and more complete archived code matter.
first_notes: The original lineage; more complete than this gutted fork, but **archived/read-only since 2020** — also unmaintained, just not deleted.

first_choose_when: Headless, unstyled primitives for building your own design system.
first_notes: Radix is lower-level (you bring your own styles); Ant Design is a complete, styled system.

project_or_alternative: RAG / vector memory stores (e.g. Mem0, Letta)
first_choose_when: Choose RAG/vector memory stores when you need durable cross-session semantic memory with embeddings.
first_notes: Durable cross-session *semantic* memory with embeddings; heavier, server/DB-backed, and aimed at long-term knowledge — Context Mode's FTS5 store is per-project, local-first, and tuned to in-session resume.

first_choose_when: Pick RAPTOR when recursive clustering plus summarization trees and embedding-time retrieval are the desired design.
first_notes: Recursive clustering + summarization tree for retrieval, but still embedding-retrieved at query time; PageIndex navigates the tree by LLM reasoning instead of vector search.

first_choose_when: Choose Rasa when you need a mature open-source conversational-AI/chatbot framework.
first_notes: Mature open-source conversational-AI/chatbot framework (intents/stories/dialogue management); more classic NLU pipeline, heavier to operate, less LLM-native guideline modeling.

first_choose_when: Choose raw `tc` when full qdisc/class/filter control is worth dealing with the steep traffic-control DSL.
first_notes: Most flexible; wondershaper is only a friendly wrapper over this engine.

first_choose_when: Choose raw ANSI escape codes when you want zero deps and only target ANSI-capable terminals.
first_notes: Zero deps and works on every ANSI-capable terminal, but breaks on legacy Windows consoles — exactly the gap colorama fills.

first_choose_when: Choose raw query dicts when zero abstraction and version-agnostic JSON matter most.
first_notes: Zero abstraction, fully version-agnostic, but verbose and refactor-hostile for complex queries — the pain the DSL exists to remove.

first_choose_when: Pick raw REST only when you want full control and accept owning OAuth refresh, pagination, and rate-limit compliance.
first_notes: Maximum control and zero abstraction, but you reimplement OAuth refresh, pagination, and rate-limit compliance yourself.

first_choose_when: Choose Raycast when you need a modern launcher with an extension store and team features.
first_notes: Modern, actively developed launcher with extensions store and team features; replaces Spotlight UX rather than injecting into it.

first_choose_when: Choose Raylib when a simple C game library with multi-language bindings fits better; choose pygame when Python tutorial gravity and SDL-style 2D workflows are the deciding factors.
first_notes: Simple C game library with bindings for many languages; very approachable, but a different ecosystem and less Python-tutorial gravity than pygame.

first_choose_when: Choose Reactour / react-joyride when you need React-specific tour components with hooks or JSX-native APIs.
first_notes: React-specific tour components (hooks/JSX-native); nicer DX inside React, but framework-locked vs Driver.js's framework-agnostic vanilla core.

first_choose_when: Choose readability-lxml when you need the Arc90 Readability port for main-content extraction only.
first_notes: Port of Arc90 Readability; main-content extraction only (no authors/date/image/NLP), smaller surface, simpler.

first_choose_when: Choose another reader extension only after checking parsing quality, license, and trust surface; choose Just Read when customization and saved selectors are the decisive feature.
first_notes: Many small clones exist; vary widely in parsing quality, licensing, and trustworthiness — Just Read's edge is its customization and selector memory.

first_choose_when: Read-later and note-taking integrations.
first_notes: Consumer read-later tools for personal knowledge management; book-to-skill targets agent harness integration, not human note-taking.

first_choose_when: Choose real Vim or Neovim when you want the full plugin ecosystem and Lua/LSP instead of IDE integration.
first_notes: The genuine article with full plugin ecosystem and Lua/LSP; but you lose JetBrains' integrated refactoring/debugger/indexing.

first_choose_when: Choose reCAPTCHA when you want a managed, free service with strong risk scoring and accept Google as a third-party dependency.
first_notes: Sends user data to Google, ships visual puzzles, and is not self-hosted. Cap keeps the flow on your infra but gives up Google-scale risk signals.

first_choose_when: Choose Redash for a lighter query-centric workflow around saved SQL and dashboards; choose Superset when visualization breadth, governance, and a richer BI surface justify the ops cost.
first_notes: Query-centric: write SQL, save queries, build dashboards from them; simpler model and lighter than Superset, but a narrower visualization set and a weaker semantic/governance layer.

first_choose_when: Choose redditdownloader when you need another dedicated Reddit downloader with a web UI.
first_notes: Another dedicated Reddit downloader with a web UI; more approachable for non-CLI users, but BDFR's scriptable CLI + YAML config suits automation better. [未验证]

first_choose_when: Choose Redis when you need the in-memory original with the richest ecosystem.
first_notes: In-memory original; lowest latency and richest command/module ecosystem, but bounded by RAM and expensive per-GB at large scale. PikiwiDB is the disk-backed capacity play, not a latency upgrade.

first_choose_when: Choose redis-rdb-tools when you need the original Python RDB parser/memory profiler.
first_notes: The original Python RDB parser/memory-profiler; broader output formats and CSV export, but much slower on large dumps and itself largely unmaintained.

first_choose_when: Choose RedisInsight when you need a full GUI with live memory analysis.
first_notes: Full GUI with a live memory analysis tab; far richer but a heavyweight desktop app talking to a live instance, not an offline file parser.

first_choose_when: Choose Redpanda Console for a Go-based Kafka/Redpanda UI, especially in Redpanda environments; choose kafka-ui only when its Java/Spring stack and feature set fit your existing deployment.
first_notes: Open-source Kafka/Redpanda UI (Go); clean, fast, works with vanilla Kafka too; some advanced features gated toward Redpanda's commercial tier.

first_choose_when: Choose Reeder when a polished paid Apple-platform reader is acceptable and closed source is not a blocker; choose NetNewsWire when free MIT code, auditability, and no monetization pressure matter more.
first_notes: Polished commercial Apple-platform reader with broad sync support; closed-source and paid, where NetNewsWire is free/MIT and auditable.

first_choose_when: Choose reflog, git stash, or manual snapshots when native tree-state recovery is enough.
first_notes: Native recovery primitives you already have, but they capture tree state only — no prompts/responses/tool-call context, no per-session indexing, no agent-aware redaction.

first_choose_when: Choose restart-plus-logging when preserving live state is less important than staying on the safe operational path.
first_notes: Safe, but it loses the in-the-moment symptom that pyrasite exists to inspect.

first_choose_when: Full-stack React framework focused on web standards, progressive enhancement, and less vendor coupling.
first_notes: Remix is less opinionated about deployment and avoids some Vercel-specific features; Next.js has more built-in optimizations (image, font, script) and a larger community.

first_choose_when: Pick Remotion directly when programmatic React video composition is enough and agent orchestration is unnecessary.
first_notes: OpenMontage embeds Remotion as one of two render backends; use Remotion directly if you only need programmatic React video composition.

first_choose_when: Choose requests + BeautifulSoup when the classic synchronous scraping combo is still enough.
first_notes: The classic, still-fine combo for simple synchronous scraping; `requests-html` is essentially this plus PyQuery selectors and an optional JS-render bolt-on, but without active maintenance.

first_choose_when: Choose requests-futures when you want `requests` compatibility with real threads and no gevent monkeypatching.
first_notes: Simpler integration for some apps, but thread-pool concurrency has different scaling and blocking tradeoffs.

first_choose_when: Choose requests-oauthlib or oauthlib when you want lower-level control over one OAuth flow; choose Authomatic when provider presets and a normalized social-login wrapper save more work.
first_notes: Lower-level OAuth client building blocks; you wire the flow yourself — more control, less convenience than Authomatic's provider presets.

first_choose_when: Choose the OpenResty-bundled copy when version matching with ngx_lua matters more than vendoring this repo directly.
first_notes: Usually how teams get the library in production.

first_choose_when: Choose Resumable.js when an older, simpler resumable upload library and legacy browser support are enough.
first_notes: Older library, not a protocol reference implementation, with a less active ecosystem than tus.

first_choose_when: Choose rich when you need styled terminal *output* such as tables, markup, progress, or syntax highlighting.
first_notes: Styled terminal *output* (tables, markup, progress, syntax) — not a full-screen UI/event loop; complementary, not a substitute for interactive screens.

first_choose_when: Choose rich when large text is only one part of a broader styled terminal-output toolkit.
first_notes: Styling library that can render large text and styled output as part of a bigger toolkit; broader but heavier if you only want art text.

first_choose_when: Choose rich when Markdown rendering is part of a larger Python styled-terminal-output toolkit.
first_notes: Python library that renders Markdown to styled terminal output as part of a larger toolkit; library-first, not a standalone CLI.

first_choose_when: Choose Rich when you need a full styled-output toolkit for color, tables, markdown, progress, and tracebacks.
first_notes: Full styled-output toolkit (color, tables, markdown, progress, traceback) — vastly more capable, but a large library; overkill if you only need cross-platform color.

first_choose_when: Choose rich.progress when you already use `rich` or need polished multi-column progress UI.
first_notes: Part of the `rich` library — far fancier (colors, columns, multiple bars, spinners, tables) and great for polished CLIs; heavier dependency and more API surface than tqdm's one-call wrap.

first_choose_when: Choose a custom YOLO + Siamese pipeline when clean licensing and full control matter more than using this repo as-is.
first_notes: You build, label, and train the whole pipeline this repo already assembles.

first_choose_when: Choose Roo Code when you want the active open-source VS Code agent Kilo Code descends from.
first_notes: Open-source VS Code agent that Kilo Code descends from [推断]; overlapping mode model. Kilo is the further-developed, org-backed continuation — but Roo Code is its own active project.

first_choose_when: Choose RQ when Redis-only simplicity matters more than broker choice, routing, scheduling, and throughput tuning.
first_notes: Dead-simple to run and read, but narrower than Celery's broker/backend and workflow surface.

first_choose_when: Choose Rust + PyO3 when the hot component should be rewritten in Rust rather than kept in a Python-superset language.
first_notes: Memory-safe and fast, but it brings a different language and toolchain.

first_choose_when: Choose mergekit passthrough when you need a general layer-stacking model-merge tool.
first_notes: mergekit's `passthrough` method also duplicates/stacks layers, but it's a general model-merging toolkit aimed at producing a finished merged model; llm-circuit-finder adds the *search* loop (sweep + probes) to discover *which* block to duplicate and validate it.

first_choose_when: Choose SAGA when terrain and raster-analysis modules are the center; choose QGIS when general-purpose desktop GIS, cartography, and editing are also required.
first_notes: Strong terrain/raster analysis library and modules; weaker cartography and general-purpose editing; also wrapped inside QGIS Processing.

first_choose_when: Choose Sarama for Go services that want a mature no-native-dependency Kafka client; choose kafka-python for the same portability tradeoff in Python.
first_notes: Mature pure-Go Kafka client; same "no native dep" appeal but for Go, not Python.

first_choose_when: Choose ScaNN when Google's anisotropic-quantization ANN library fits your CPU workload.
first_notes: Google's anisotropic-quantization ANN library, very strong recall/latency on CPU; narrower index menu and ecosystem than FAISS, no first-class GPU build.

first_choose_when: Choose SciPy, OR-Tools, or Gurobi when you need exact, convex, or MILP solvers.
first_notes: Exact/convex/MILP solvers; the right tool when your problem is structured (linear/convex/integer-programming), where EAs are the wrong hammer.

first_choose_when: Choose Scrapy when you need a maintained crawling framework with a login middleware pattern.
first_notes: A maintained crawling framework with a login middleware pattern; you write the auth, but everything around it is production-grade.

first_choose_when: Choose Scrapy plus custom extraction rules when you need a full crawling framework.
first_notes: Full crawling framework — you write extraction rules but get queuing, concurrency, retries, pipelines; the right tool when you need a *crawler*, not a one-URL extractor.

first_choose_when: Lower-level scraping frameworks.
first_notes: Scrapy and Playwright give full control but require building and maintaining crawler infrastructure.

first_choose_when: Choose scrapy-rotating-proxies when you already have a proxy list and only need Scrapy rotation middleware.
first_notes: A Scrapy *downloader middleware* that rotates a list you supply and bans dead ones — it consumes proxies, it does not source/validate them; pair it with a pool like this one rather than treat it as a substitute.

first_choose_when: Choose Scrapy proxy middleware when you already have the proxy list and only need rotation.
first_notes: Library middleware that rotates a *list you supply* inside Scrapy; complements rather than competes — it doesn't harvest proxies, it consumes them.

first_choose_when: Choose ScrapydWeb when you need a more featureful web UI over Scrapyd.
first_notes: More featureful web UI over Scrapyd (multi-node, log parsing, email alerts), but itself also fairly stale.

first_choose_when: Choose ScrapydWeb or Gerapy when you need richer admin UIs over Scrapyd.
first_notes: Also admin UIs over Scrapyd: ScrapydWeb adds multi-node/log-parsing/alerts; Gerapy is Django+Vue and more modern. Both call Scrapyd's API, not replacements for the daemon.

first_choose_when: Choose Seafile when reliable two-way sync, delta sync, and client apps are mandatory; keep copyparty for ad hoc uploads and multi-protocol serving where sync is explicitly not required.
first_notes: Block-based sync-and-share with strong delta sync and client apps. copyparty wins on portability/zero-deps and protocol breadth (WebDAV/FTP/SFTP/TFTP/SMB) but has no real sync.

project_or_alternative: Security MCP servers (e.g. tool-wrapping SIEM/scanner MCPs)
first_choose_when: Choose security MCP servers when live tool access with structured I/O is the missing piece.
first_notes: Give the agent live *tool access* with structured I/O; this pack gives *procedural knowledge*, not connectivity. Complementary, not substitutes — one knows the steps, the other can execute against a system.

first_choose_when: Choose selectolax when you need a very fast C-backed HTML parser with CSS selectors.
first_notes: Very fast C-backed (Modest/lexbor) HTML parser with CSS selectors; parsing only (bring your own HTTP client), but the speed choice for large documents — what `requests-html` is not.

first_choose_when: Build your own only when encryption, schema, or security constraints make paperless-ngx unacceptable; otherwise paperless-ngx buys you a maintained ingest/OCR/index/UI pipeline.
first_notes: Maximum flexibility and full control over encryption/schema, but you build and maintain the whole ingest/OCR/index/UI pipeline — worth it only when paperless's data model or security constraints are dealbreakers.

first_choose_when: DIY stack matching Supabase's components.
first_notes: More flexible and fully self-managed, but requires significantly more setup and ongoing maintenance than Supabase's integrated platform.

first_choose_when: Choose Semgrep when reproducible rule IDs, SARIF, local/free runs, and community rules matter more than LLM context; choose this tool when logic-level security reasoning over a trusted PR diff is the gap.
first_notes: Deterministic, rule-based SAST with SARIF and a huge community ruleset; fast, free, reproducible — but pattern-bound, weaker on logic/contextual bugs.

first_choose_when: Choose sentence-transformers when you need the upstream library text2vec builds on.
first_notes: The upstream library text2vec builds on; broader model zoo and English/multilingual coverage, but less Chinese-curated out of the box and no bundled BM25/Word2Vec convenience.

first_choose_when: Choose Serena when you need an LSP-backed semantic code MCP server for agents.
first_notes: LSP-backed semantic code MCP server for agents; symbol/LSP-driven rather than a persisted Tree-sitter graph with blast-radius + community/risk analysis.

first_choose_when: Commercial proxy clients.
first_notes: Shadowrocket (iOS) and Surge (macOS/iOS) are paid, closed-source apps with broader platform support.

project_or_alternative: Shape Up book / BaseCamp's own materials
first_choose_when: Choose the source materials when you need methodology prose rather than installable agent skills.
first_notes: The source methodology as prose, not an installable agent skill — this pack is one person's operationalization of it inside Claude Code.

first_choose_when: Shotcut is built on MLT. Use Shotcut when you want a ready-made open-source NLE; use MLT directly when you need to embed or extend the engine.
first_notes: The open-source NLE built on MLT; reach for it when you need an editor, not a framework.

first_choose_when: Choose Showdown only when maintaining legacy code that already depends on it.
first_notes: Older JS markdown converter; less active, less spec-compliant, and generally superseded by markdown-it or marked.

first_choose_when: Choose Sidekiq or BullMQ when the same background-job problem lives in Ruby or Node instead of Python.
first_notes: Same problem shape, different language ecosystem.

first_choose_when: Choose SigLIP when you need a newer image-text model trained with a sigmoid loss.
first_notes: Newer image-text model trained with a sigmoid loss; typically stronger zero-shot accuracy and better at scale, but a different model family — usually consumed via OpenCLIP or `transformers`, not this repo.

first_choose_when: Choose SikuliX when Java-based image recognition automation with OCR and template matching is acceptable.
first_notes: Cross-platform like PyAutoGUI but heavier because of the JVM and more IDE-centric.

first_choose_when: Next-gen proxy platform with a GUI.
first_notes: sing-box is more protocol-flexible but Clash Verge Rev has deeper Clash ecosystem compatibility.

first_choose_when: Choose a one-off prompt when the task does not need persistence, versioning, or named loading.
first_notes: A one-off prompt is the lightest possible option for one task, but it doesn't persist, version, or load by name across sessions the way an installed skill does.

first_choose_when: Choose Slidev when you need a developer-grade Markdown-to-HTML deck framework.
first_notes: Developer-grade Markdown→HTML deck framework with build tooling, themes, and a dev server; more powerful/long-stable but not agent-driven and not opinionated about Swiss/editorial aesthetics.

first_choose_when: Choose SmolVLM when explicitly tiny on-device VLMs are the priority.
first_notes: Explicitly tiny VLMs for on-device; comparable "small + multimodal" niche, often even smaller, but typically less capable on video and a narrower model lineup than MiniCPM-V's generations.

first_choose_when: Choose SnowNLP or cnsenti when you need lightweight Chinese sentiment libraries.
first_notes: Lightweight Chinese sentiment libraries (lexicon/classic ML); trivial to run, far weaker than pretrained transformers — opposite end of the accuracy/effort tradeoff.

first_choose_when: Choose Snyk Code when a managed commercial security dashboard and dependency scanning are part of the requirement; choose this tool for a repo-local OSS Action driven by Claude review comments.
first_notes: Commercial ML/SAST with a managed dashboard and dependency scanning; hosted SaaS, not a single-repo OSS Action.

first_choose_when: Fine-grained reactive UI library with no virtual DOM and excellent performance.
first_notes: Solid is even more performance-focused with a smaller community; Svelte has a larger ecosystem, SvelteKit, and a gentler learning curve.

first_choose_when: Choose Sourcegraph or SCIP when you need mature multi-repo code intelligence at scale.
first_notes: Mature, multi-repo code intelligence and indexing at scale; heavier infra, not a local single-binary MCP context-reducer aimed at agent token budgets.

first_choose_when: Choose transcript exporters when exported chat logs are enough.
first_notes: Other tools also persist agent chat transcripts, but typically as exported files/markdown rather than Git-checkpoint provenance tied to commits with a rewind mechanism. Verify feature parity before substituting.

first_choose_when: Choose Spring Batch when the need is chunked read/process/write batch processing and restartability, not scheduling.
first_notes: Complementary, not a substitute; you still need something to trigger it.

first_choose_when: Choose SSDB when you need an older LevelDB-backed Redis-like disk store.
first_notes: Older LevelDB-backed Redis-ish disk store; similar idea, smaller/aging community and weaker protocol fidelity than PikiwiDB.

first_choose_when: Ionic's Web Components compiler — compiles to standards-compliant custom elements.
first_notes: Stencil is a compile-time toolchain; Lit is a runtime library. Stencil is better for generating component libraries from decorated classes; Lit is simpler for direct use.

first_choose_when: Choose streamlink or yt-dlp when you need full stream-download tools that parse HLS internally.
first_notes: Full stream-download tools that parse HLS internally; use them to *grab* a stream, not as a library to *manipulate* manifests in your own code. [未验证]

first_choose_when: Choose Stylelint when you need deterministic CSS linting with a large rule ecosystem.
first_notes: Deterministic CSS linting with a huge rule ecosystem; targets CSS correctness/conventions, not aesthetic AI-pattern detection or agent design coaching.

first_choose_when: Fast, lightweight proprietary editor.
first_notes: Sublime is faster and lighter but proprietary and paid; VS Code is free and open-source.

first_choose_when: Choose subprocess + raw ffmpeg when you need zero dependency and total control.
first_notes: Zero dependency and total control, but you hand-build and escape the `-filter_complex` strings yourself — the pain this library removes.

first_choose_when: Choose Subtitle Edit when you need a full GUI subtitle editor with manual and automatic sync.
first_notes: Full GUI subtitle editor with manual + automatic sync, OCR, and format conversion; far broader, but interactive and Windows-centric rather than a scriptable one-shot CLI.

first_choose_when: Use RustDesk for general-purpose self-hosted remote desktop; choose Sunshine + Moonlight when you need low-latency game streaming or high-frame-rate remote desktop.
first_notes: Open-source game-streaming host (Sunshine) and client (Moonlight) optimized for low latency and high FPS; narrower use case than general remote desktop.

first_choose_when: Choose SvelteKit when you want Svelte's full-stack meta-framework rather than a standalone component framework.
first_notes: SvelteKit adds routing, SSR, and app conventions around Svelte; Angular remains more enterprise-opinionated and longer-established.

first_choose_when: Choose Swift when the ModelScope ecosystem is the stronger fit for a broad fine-tuning framework.
first_notes: Broadly overlapping scope; ecosystem preference is the deciding tradeoff.

first_choose_when: Use Warp for a polished, commercially supported AI terminal; choose Tabby when you want a modern, open-source terminal with SSH client and serial support.
first_notes: Open source and cross-platform, with some modern UI features, but less AI-native than Warp.

first_choose_when: Choose Tableau or Power BI when mature commercial visuals, data prep, and enterprise support outweigh cost and lock-in; choose Superset for self-hosted open-source BI.
first_notes: Proprietary, commercial BI with mature visuals, data prep, and enterprise support; richer polish and ecosystem, but licensing cost, vendor lock-in, and (for Power BI) Microsoft-stack gravity — not self-hosted open source.

first_choose_when: Choose Taskmaster when you need another popular PRD-to-tasks agent workflow.
first_notes: Popular PRD-to-tasks agent workflow; parses a spec into tasks too, but is its own task store/CLI rather than syncing to GitHub Issues + git worktrees as the shared truth.

first_choose_when: Choose Taskwarrior when you need a battle-tested offline CLI task manager.
first_notes: Battle-tested offline CLI task manager with rich filtering, but no SQL/version-control backend, weaker multi-agent merge story, not built around agent JSON workflows.

first_choose_when: Use RustDesk for self-hosted, open-source remote desktop; choose TeamViewer when you need a commercial, cloud-managed remote desktop with enterprise support and cross-platform reliability.
first_notes: Commercial, cloud-managed remote desktop with enterprise support, session recording, and compliance; requires paid subscription and routes data through their cloud.

first_choose_when: Choose Teedy when a Java stack, document versioning, and modest resource needs take priority; keep paperless-ngx when OCR and auto-tagging automation are the deciding features.
first_notes: Lightweight Java DMS with versioning, clean UI and modest resource needs; weaker automated OCR/auto-tagging and smaller momentum.

first_choose_when: Choose Temporal for durable, long-running, stateful code workflows with signals, retries, and timers rather than batch DAG scheduling.
first_notes: Durable-execution engine for long-running, stateful, code-driven workflows (signals, retries, timers); not a batch *scheduler* with a DAG UI — a different orchestration shape entirely.

first_choose_when: Choose termcolor / colored when you need tiny ANSI color helpers with friendly APIs but no legacy-Windows ANSI translation.
first_notes: Tiny ANSI color helpers with friendly APIs, but don't translate ANSI on legacy Windows — often paired *with* colorama for that.

first_choose_when: Choose texify when you want a more recently maintained open-source equation-to-LaTeX model; choose pix2tex only after benchmarking accuracy and accepting its coasting maintenance state.
first_notes: Open-source equation-to-LaTeX model (VikParuchuri); a more recently-maintained direct alternative aimed at the same task — worth comparing on your data and on maintenance recency.

first_choose_when: Choose TGI when you need Hugging Face's production server and tight HF ecosystem integration.
first_notes: Hugging Face's production server, tight HF ecosystem integration; license history has wobbled (Apache→HFOIL→Apache), narrower than a full compiler+language platform.

first_choose_when: Pick TextGrad when textual-gradient optimization is the mechanism you want to explore.
first_notes: Also optimizes LM pipelines, via "textual gradients" / backprop-through-text; narrower module model than DSPy's signatures+optimizers.

first_choose_when: Python library for extracting text from many formats.
first_notes: Older project with broader format support but less focus on Markdown structure preservation for LLMs.

first_choose_when: Choose Textual when you need a modern async, CSS-styled, mouse-first TUI framework.
first_notes: Modern async, CSS-styled, mouse-first TUI framework (Textualize); much richer widget/styling model and active backing, but heavier and a different programming model than asciimatics' curses-like API.

first_choose_when: Fast grep replacement with gitignore support, written in C.
first_notes: ag is mature and fast; ripgrep is generally faster, has better Unicode support, and more active maintenance.

first_choose_when: Choose community knowledge-work packs when breadth and velocity outweigh first-party provenance.
first_notes: Larger, faster-moving office/comms bundles, but no Anthropic curation or provenance guarantee. This repo is the first-party baseline; community packs extend it at higher trust cost.

project_or_alternative: Third-party Claude Code marketplaces / community plugin lists
first_choose_when: Choose community plugin lists when breadth and velocity outweigh first-party provenance.
first_notes: Larger surface and faster-moving, but no Anthropic curation or provenance guarantee. This repo is the first-party baseline; community marketplaces extend it at higher trust cost.

first_choose_when: Choose thriftpy2 when you need the maintained runtime-load-`.thrift` successor and are leaving this archived repo.
first_notes: Same model with current Python support; the direct migration target.

first_choose_when: Use RustDesk for self-hosted, open-source remote desktop with modern encryption; choose TightVNC when you need a traditional VNC server for LAN-based remote access without encryption by default.
first_notes: Traditional VNC for LAN access; simple and protocol-standard but lacks modern encryption, NAT traversal, and mobile clients without extra setup.

first_choose_when: Choose Nixtla when you need hosted forecasting API plus classical/neural OSS forecasting libs.
first_notes: Hosted/managed forecasting API and OSS libs (statsforecast/neuralforecast). Nixtla's classical/neural libs are great when per-series training is fine; TimesFM trades that for zero-shot.

first_choose_when: Use Excalidraw for the de-facto standard hand-drawn whiteboard; choose tldraw when you want a newer, more extensible whiteboard library with a stronger dev-focused API.
first_notes: Newer whiteboard library with strong programmatic API; smaller ecosystem but more flexible for custom apps.

first_choose_when: Choose token-saving MCP servers when you only need to shrink tool payloads.
first_notes: Other MCP servers that shrink tool payloads; narrower (truncate/summarize) and typically single-platform vs Context Mode's execute-sandbox + session-continuity + 17-platform routing.

first_choose_when: Choose torchgan when you need an importable GAN library/framework with trainers, losses, and metrics.
first_notes: An actual GAN *library/framework* (modular trainers, losses, metrics) you import and configure; better if you want reusable building blocks, less suited to reading one paper's architecture end-to-end.

first_choose_when: Choose torchtune when PyTorch-native fine-tuning/RL recipes are enough and an agent-RL framework would be too opinionated.
first_notes: A building block in this ecosystem, not a complete agent-rollout training framework.

first_choose_when: Choose Tour of Go when the goal is guided learning rather than running your own exploratory notebook code.
first_notes: Curated and interactive, but fixed-content rather than a reusable kernel.

first_choose_when: Choose tracemalloc when you control the code and can instrument allocation tracking from inside the target process.
first_notes: Built into CPython and maintained, but it cannot attach to an arbitrary already-running PID.

first_choose_when: Choose Traefik when Kubernetes/container auto-discovery and lightweight file/CRD config beat plugin breadth; choose Kong for a heavier programmable policy gateway.
first_notes: Go reverse proxy with strong container/Kubernetes auto-discovery and a file/CRD config model; lighter to run but a thinner policy/AI-gateway plugin story.

first_choose_when: Choose trafilatura when you need a modern maintained Python extractor with strong benchmarks and metadata.
first_notes: Modern, maintained Python extractor with strong benchmarks and metadata; usually the better default now — different language.

first_choose_when: Choose Trivy or Grype when you need to report CVEs or produce SBOMs rather than shrink images.
first_notes: Find and report CVEs / produce SBOMs; they *measure* attack surface, they don't *shrink* it. Complementary, not a substitute.

first_choose_when: Choose TrOCR for transformer-based line recognition, handwriting, or hard single-line cases; choose Tesseract when page-level formats, language packs, and CPU-only operation are the core requirement.
first_notes: Transformer (encoder-decoder) OCR from Microsoft; strong on handwriting and hard lines, but model-heavy and GPU-oriented, and it is line-level recognition without Tesseract's full page/format tooling.

first_choose_when: This is the *client* companion, not a server alternative. You use tus-js-client in the browser to talk to tusd.
first_notes: A client library, not a substitute. It pairs with tusd (or any tus server).

first_choose_when: Pick Tushare when you accept token/points gating for a long-standing Chinese markets data source.
first_notes: Long-standing Chinese financial-data library (much of it token/points-gated now); strong on markets data, more commercial gating than gopup.

first_choose_when: Choose Tyk when a Go gateway with open-source dashboard, developer portal, and multi-tenancy is the priority; choose Kong for broader plugin depth and OpenResty/Lua extensibility.
first_notes: Go-based, ships a dashboard + developer portal + multi-tenancy in its open-source stack; narrower raw-proxy throughput and plugin count than Kong.

first_choose_when: Choose enterprise RPA tools when you need governed desktop-plus-web automation.
first_notes: Enterprise desktop+web RPA with governance — but proprietary, costly, vendor lock-in, heavyweight vs a JS snippet.

first_choose_when: Pick unstructured.io when you want the broader RAG-loader ecosystem and accept an OSS core plus commercial service split.
first_notes: Broad multi-format document loader popular for RAG ingestion with many partitioners; open-source core plus a commercial API/service tier — capability split and licensing differ from Docling's single MIT library.

first_choose_when: Choose Uppy when the missing piece is the browser upload UI, not the resumable upload server.
first_notes: Polished widget with many plugins; often pairs with tusd, but is not a server replacement.

first_choose_when: Choose urwid when you need a long-established Python console UI library with flexible widgets and layouts.
first_notes: Long-established Python console UI library with a flexible widget/layout system; Unix-focused (weaker Windows story) and no animation engine.

first_choose_when: Pick v0 when the target is hosted prompt-to-web-UI generation rather than a local multi-artifact studio.
first_notes: Hosted prompt-to-UI generator; cloud SaaS, narrower to web UI, vs Open Design's local multi-artifact studio.

project_or_alternative: v0 / Lovable / other AI UI generators
first_choose_when: Pick hosted AI UI generators when you want competing design-to-code products rather than agent skills.
first_notes: Competing AI design-to-code products, mostly hosted SaaS rather than agent-skill repos; different unit of consumption (you drive their UI, not your agent).

first_choose_when: Choose Vector when you need a Rust observability pipeline with strong transform DSL support.
first_notes: Rust observability pipeline (logs/metrics) with strong transform DSL (VRL); comparable single-binary routing, smaller plugin catalog for exotic inputs.

first_choose_when: Choose Velocity.js only for legacy compatibility with an existing jQuery-era codebase; choose Anime.js for actively maintained modern vanilla animation.
first_notes: Older jQuery-era JS animator, now largely unmaintained. Anime.js is the actively maintained modern equivalent.

first_choose_when: Choose verl when you need the underlying distributed RL engine Agent Lightning builds on.
first_notes: Powerful, but expects you to express training as its generation loop rather than wrap a native agent.

first_choose_when: Choose Vibe Kanban when you need a board-first UX for orchestrating multiple coding agents.
first_notes: Kanban-style board for orchestrating multiple coding agents; overlapping "supervise many agents" goal with a board-first UX rather than a worktree-daemon + feedback-loop emphasis.

first_choose_when: Use VLC for a standalone media player with broad format support.
first_notes: End-user player, not a framework for building your own app.

first_choose_when: Choose vscode-neovim when you need a *real* Neovim instance embedded inside VS Code.
first_notes: Embeds a *real* Neovim instance inside VS Code for higher fidelity + your Neovim config; heavier and VS Code-only, no JetBrains equivalent of this depth.

first_choose_when: Choose VSCodeVim when VS Code is your editor and you only need Vim emulation there.
first_notes: Vim emulation for VS Code; same idea on a different host — choose by which IDE you actually use, not by the plugin.

first_choose_when: Fully open-source build of VS Code without Microsoft telemetry.
first_notes: VSCodium removes telemetry but lacks the Microsoft extensions marketplace and some proprietary features.

first_choose_when: Pure WebAssembly runtimes.
first_notes: These are for Wasm modules, not JS/TS applications; Deno can run Wasm but is primarily a JS runtime.

first_choose_when: Use Whisper when you need end-to-end multilingual transcription + translation out of the box; choose Wav2Vec 2.0 when you need fine-grained phonetic analysis or custom-domain fine-tuning with Meta's research tooling.
first_notes: Meta's research speech models; excellent for academic and fine-tuning workflows but not a turnkey transcription product.

first_choose_when: Choose raw WAAPI when you want no library and can tolerate low-level code; choose Anime.js when you need timeline, stagger, SVG, and ergonomic sequencing on top.
first_notes: Native browser API, no library to ship; lower-level, no timeline/stagger/SVG-morph sugar. Anime.js v4 includes a WAAPI adapter and adds the ergonomic layer on top.

first_choose_when: Choose Webmin when you need an older, broader Perl-based control panel across many services and init systems.
first_notes: Older, broader Perl-based control panel covering many services (mail, DNS, Apache, BIND) on multiple init systems; heavier and less "live session" — Cockpit is leaner, systemd-native, and reflects real-time OS state.

project_or_alternative: WeChat Official Account / Mini-Program server APIs
first_choose_when: Choose official account or mini-program APIs for supported public-account automation.
first_notes: Official server-side APIs for *public accounts* and mini-programs; fully supported but a different product surface (broadcast/service accounts), not personal 1:1 IM automation.

first_choose_when: Choose WeChatTweak-macOS when you insist on a macOS WeChat tweak and want a newer successor.
first_notes: The community successor for macOS WeChat tweaks — same anti-revoke/multi-instance class of features, but more recently maintained and with a CLI installer; still a binary patch against a specific WeChat version, so it inherits the same version-fragility and ToS/ban exposure. The more sensible pick if you insist on this approach.

first_choose_when: Choose wechaty when a maintained multi-language bot framework is worth the puppet risk.
first_notes: Actively-maintained multi-language (TS/Python/Go/Java) conversational-bot framework with pluggable "puppets"; the de-facto successor for personal-account-style WeChat bots, but still rides on unofficial/3rd-party access channels and the same ToS/ban exposure — pick a puppet carefully.

first_choose_when: Choose official Tencent automation surfaces when legitimate enterprise/public automation fits.
first_notes: Tencent's **official, sanctioned** automation surfaces; stable and supported, but they automate enterprise/public-account contexts, not your personal desktop WeChat — a legitimate but different product, not a drop-in.

first_choose_when: Choose WeCom when official enterprise messaging automation is acceptable.
first_notes: Tencent's **official, sanctioned** enterprise messaging API; stable and supported, but it automates *WeCom* accounts/contacts, not arbitrary personal WeChat accounts — a different (legitimate) surface, not a drop-in replacement.

first_choose_when: Use Alacritty for minimal, raw-performance GPU terminal emulation; choose WezTerm when you want a modern GPU-accelerated terminal with tabs, splits, and ligatures built in.
first_notes: WezTerm has more built-in features (tabs, ligatures, multiplexing); Alacritty is faster and more minimal.

first_choose_when: Use Whisper when you need the Python/PyTorch reference or the most flexible scripting; choose whisper.cpp when you need portable, CPU-optimized inference on laptops, mobile, or edge devices.
first_notes: Georgi Gerganov's C++ port (the llama.cpp author). Extremely popular for on-device and edge deployment; pure C++ with no Python/PyTorch dependency.

first_choose_when: Choose the Wikipedia guide when you need the reference source, not an installable skill.
first_notes: The reference source behind the rubric — a human-readable guide, not an installable skill. Use it to audit or extend the checklist, not to run edits.

first_choose_when: Use Alacritty for cross-platform, minimal GPU terminal emulation; choose Windows Terminal when you want Microsoft's modern terminal for Windows with tabs and GPU acceleration.
first_notes: Windows Terminal is Windows-only and integrates with WSL; Alacritty is cross-platform and simpler.

first_choose_when: Platform-native UI toolkits.
first_notes: True native widgets and performance, but each platform requires separate codebases and expertise.

project_or_alternative: Your harness's built-in review / simplify commands
first_choose_when: Prefer built-ins when generic diff review is enough and you do not need Dimillian's Apple-specific skills.
first_notes: Codex/Claude already ship generic diff-review and simplify flows; the generic skills here (`review-swarm`, `review-and-simplify-changes`) overlap with those — the unique value is the SwiftUI/iOS skills, not the generic ones.

project_or_alternative: Your own global `CLAUDE.md` / Anthropic built-in guidance
first_choose_when: Do not add this pack if your existing global agent instructions already cover the same behavior.
first_notes: If you already maintain opinionated global agent instructions, that's the same surface; this would be additive prose competing for the same context.

first_choose_when: Choose a fresh PyTorch baseline when you want the same fixed-length idea on current tooling.
first_notes: Cleaner than reviving abandoned code, but you write it from scratch and use this repo only as a reference.

first_choose_when: Choose YouTube Data API captions when you need the official contractual API and have the required ownership/OAuth.
first_notes: Official and contractual, but requires OAuth and (for caption *download*) channel ownership — you generally can't pull arbitrary third-party caption text, which is exactly this library's niche.

first_choose_when: Pick Zapier when zero self-hosting and managed SaaS convenience matter more than code escape hatches.
first_notes: Zapier requires no setup but is proprietary, cloud-only, and charges per task; n8n is self-hostable and code-extensible.

first_choose_when: Choose Zep when temporal knowledge-graph memory is the main architecture bet.
first_notes: Temporal knowledge-graph memory service with a strong self-host/OSS core; comparable structured-memory ambition, different graph-first model.

first_choose_when: Choose Zep or Graphiti when temporal knowledge-graph memory and fact invalidation are central.
first_notes: Temporal knowledge-graph memory service with explicit fact invalidation; a hosted/self-host backend for app memory, not a per-developer coding-agent hook layer.

first_choose_when: Choose zkui or zk-web when you need a web-based multi-user ZooKeeper UI.
first_notes: Web-based ZooKeeper UIs (deploy as a service, multi-user) rather than a desktop app; different deployment model.

first_choose_when: Choose ZoeDepth when you need metric monocular depth with absolute scale.
first_notes: Metric monocular depth; a direct alternative when you specifically need absolute scale rather than relative depth.

first_choose_when: Choose ZooInspector when you need the classic Swing-based ZooKeeper GUI.
first_notes: The classic Swing-based ZK GUI; older and clunkier UI, but historically the reference desktop inspector.

first_choose_when: Choose zstd when you need the general-purpose compression baseline.
first_notes: The general-purpose baseline (also Meta/BSD). Excellent ratio-at-speed on arbitrary bytes; OpenZL targets *beating* it on specific structured formats via format awareness, at the cost of having to describe the data.

first_choose_when: Choose Zyte Scrapy Cloud when you need commercial managed SaaS for Scrapy.
first_notes: Commercial managed SaaS for Scrapy (no self-hosting); removes ops at the cost of vendor lock-in and per-usage pricing.
